latest.title: Factors influencing consumer choice in the informal food retail markets in Ghana
latest.venue: African Journal of Economic and Management Studies
latest.abstract: Purpose The study sought to investigate the factors influencing consumer choice in the informal food retail market. Design/methodology/approach Using a descriptive research design and quantitative methodology, 432 useable questionnaires were obtained from respondents through a convenience sampling method from Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi and Koforidua. The study employed exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis and discriminant validity before conducting the structural equation model to examine why consumers choose informal food retail as their preferred market for shopping. Findings The study established that there exists a positive statistical relationship between the environment and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.258; p-value <0.001), price and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.105; p-value = 0.017), convenience and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.175; p-value <0.001), and food variety and the informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.223; p-value <0.001). Therefore, the study concludes that consumers' choice of the informal food retail market is based on the environment, price, convenience and food variety. Research limitations/implications The study was limited to the major cities in Ghana, namely Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi and Koforidua. It was conducted as a quantitative research study. The study recommends that future research should assess differences in the selection of informal food retail markets based on demographic profiles (gender, age group and occupation) and include other cities in Ghana. Practical implications Policy makers should improve infrastructure, sanitation and promote diverse, local food options to attract more customers and foster community loyalty. latest.title: Which gambling harm prevention messages appear the most effective? Results of an online experiment comparing self-appraisal, positive emotional, loss-based and counter-industry approaches
latest.abstract: Gambling harm prevention messages are increasingly catching up with best practices from tobacco by utilizing independently designed warnings. Australia was the first country to impose this policy, using messages from three persuasion strategies: ‘loss-based’ messages warn of the likelihood of losing money, ‘self-appraisal’ messages prompt self-reflection of gambling behaviors and a ‘positive emotional’ message highlights the benefits of not gambling. In the present online experiment (N = 3,486), we compared four well-performing messages from each of these classes against four well-performing ‘counter-industry’ messages, which highlight the industry’s role in gambling harms. Messages were compared across six self-report outcomes (e.g., ‘this message makes me want to gamble less’) and based on the sentiment of optional free-text comments via a natural language processing analysis. Messages were ranked based on the overall sample and the high-risk sub-sample according to the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI). Overall, one message of each class appeared best, with positive emotional and self-appraisal messages appearing better suited to high-PGSI audiences, and loss-based messages to low-PGSI audiences. Counter-industry messages performed similarly among all audiences, but longer counter-industry messages performed worse in sentiment-based analysis. These findings inform future theory-informed message development and campaign implementation.

When Brands Matter Less: Perceived Product Similarity and Brand Switching Intention through Brand Relevance in Makassar's Grab-and-Go Coffee Market
latest.venue: Journal of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises
latest.abstract: Affordable grab-and-go coffee outlets in Makassar, Indonesia, increasingly sell comparable drinks at nearly identical prices, raising the question of whether brands still matter when products look alike. This study examines whether perceived product similarity increases brand switching intention by reducing brand relevance, that is, the importance consumers attach to brands when choosing within a category. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 250 consumers domiciled in Makassar who had a usual coffee brand and had tried at least one alternative in the same price range. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with 10,000 bootstrap subsamples. Perceived product similarity reduced brand relevance, and lower brand relevance increased brand switching intention. The resulting indirect effect of similarity on switching intention through brand relevance was positive and significant, whereas the direct effect was small and only marginally significant. The findings were robust to controlling for variety seeking, which influenced switching intention independently. The study shows that product similarity encourages switching mainly by weakening the role of the brand in consumers' choices rather than by acting on switching directly, which helps explain why earlier studies of brand parity and loyalty have reported inconsistent results. For small coffee businesses competing in a crowded price band, the results suggest that building distinctive reasons to choose the brand, such as a signature taste and consistent quality, is more effective for retaining customers than competing on price alone.

latest.title: What catches the eye: visual attention and packaging cues in consumer decision-making on potting soils
latest.abstract: Gardening is a popular hobby that offers societal and economic benefits, with potting soils as a key product. However, retailing them as low-involvement, credence goods poses several challenges. To address these and broaden the discourse on the visual perception of sustainable products at the point of sale, we examined the decision-making behavior of 273 hobby gardeners in Germany, conducting a combined approach of eye tracking and a quantitative survey at a simulated point of sale. Theoretically, we drew on the theory of visual attention and cue utilization theory. Our study indicates that consumers follow distinct behavioral phases when evaluating potting soils at the point of sale: a quick overview phase, followed by closer inspection of individual products. Our results indicate correlation between the stated importance of product attributes and their perception on the selected product. However, actual visual behavior reveals a discrepancy between both. Although attributes like application instructions are self-reported as important, this rarely leads to actual actions, such as turning over packaging. Visual attention varies notably depending on the type of cue—for example, price and graphics, which are viewed with different frequency and intensity. These findings offer valuable insights for produ​cers and policymakers: not only the informational content, such as peat-related information, but also the visual presentation on packaging significantly influences consumer attention and decision-making. Understanding how visual cues shape purchasing behavior can improve package design and communication strategies, particularly for low-involvement, credence products like potting soils.

latest.title: ОЗДОРОВЧЕ ХАРЧУВАННЯ ЯК СТРАТЕГІЧНИЙ НАПРЯМ РОЗВИТКУ СУЧАСНИХ ЗАКЛАДІВ РЕСТОРАННОГО ГОСПОДАРСТВА
latest.abstract: The article examines healthy nutrition as a strategic direction for the development of modern food service establishments amid growing consumer demand for a healthy lifestyle. The main trends in the transformation of the restaurant business, driven by changing population's eating habits, increased attention to product quality and safety, as well as the popularization of functional and dietary nutrition concepts, are considered. The factors influencing the formation of the assortment policy of food service establishments, taking into account the principles of healthy nutrition, are investigated. World and domestic experience in implementing healthy nutrition concepts in the activities of restaurant enterprises is analyzed. It is substantiated that the integration of healthy nutrition principles into the development strategy of a food service establishment contributes to enhancing the enterprise's competitiveness, forming a positive image and consumer loyalty, and opens up new opportunities for business diversification. Practical recommendations for developing a strategy for the development of food service establishments based on the principles of healthy nutrition, covering the marketing, technological, and personnel components of the enterprise's activities, are proposed. A necessary condition for the effective functioning of catering establishments oriented toward the specified segment is ensuring transparency and accessibility of information about the range of products, their composition, nutritional value, and compliance with certain dietary principles. In particular, information about dietary, vegetarian, vegan, and other specialized dishes should be presented in the menus of establishments, on official web resources, and digital ordering platforms. latest.title: The Gap Between What Consumers Say They Want and What They Actually Buy
latest.abstract: Businesses spend a lot of time asking customers what they want. Surveys, feedback forms and sales conversations all try to answer that one question. Yet what people say they want and what they finally buy are often not the same thing. This paper looks at why that gap exists and what it means for marketers and salespeople. It focuses on high-involvement purchases such as homes and eyewear, where the decision is costly, personal, or both. The study follows a secondary research approach and draws on published work in consumer psychology, marketing and retail. The author’s internship experience at a real estate consultancy, BlisssRed Pvt. Ltd., and a case study of Lenskart are used as practical illustrations, not as proof. The paper looks at intention–behaviour research, the way preferences are formed at the moment of choice, and the effect of price, choice overload, trust, channels and follow-up. The paper finds that the gap does not mean customers are dishonest. Most people are sincere when they state a preference. But needs are often unclear at the start, preferences shift as options appear, and practical limits such as budget, timing and risk take over at the point of purchase. Businesses that keep asking, watch what customers actually do, and give honest guidance are better placed to close the gap than those that rely on one survey or one conversation.

latest.title: Sustainability over social responsibility in evaluations of hotel choice: An eye-tracking research note
latest.abstract: Sustainability and social responsibility have become increasingly influential factors shaping consumer decision-making in the tourism and hospitality sector. Following a broadened version of norm activation model and the construal level theory, the present experimental eye-tracking study examines whether sustainability elements on hotel websites have a greater influence on hotel selection than social responsibility messages. A total of 138 participants (83 women, 55 men) viewed hotel website stimuli that contained sustainability and social responsibility banners. They were then asked which hotel they would choose to reserve and what they considered important for their choice. Participants allocated comparable visual attention to the sustainability banner and the social responsibility banner. Interestingly, greater visual attention to the sustainability banner was positively associated with higher self-reported importance of sustainability information in hotel choice. For the social responsibility banner, the association was in the same positive direction but non-significant. This discrepancy between attentional and evaluative processes may be explained by the psychological concept of psychological distance. Sustainability is suggested to be closer to the consumer’s immediate experience “here and now” during the hotel stay, e.g. eco-friendly cleaning approach, energy efficiency. In contrast, consumers may view socially responsible actions, such as supporting the local community, as more distant or less immediate.

latest.title: Influence of Digital Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Financial Decision-Making
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has significantly changed the way consumers discover, evaluate, and choose financial products and services. The growing use of social media, search engines, online advertisements, influencer promotions, and digital financial platforms has created new opportunities for financial institutions to connect with customers. However, concerns regarding data privacy, misleading promotions, online security, and the credibility of digital information make consumer trust an important consideration. This research paper examines the influence of digital marketing on consumer behaviour and financial decision-making, focusing on awareness, preferences, trust, perceived risk, and financial product selection. The study adopts a secondary research approach, drawing on academic studies, research papers, industry reports, official publications, and credible online sources. It examines how digital marketing shapes consumer perceptions and influences financial product selection, with particular attention to digital communication, personalised advertising, social media engagement, and online information. It also considers how financial awareness and familiarity with digital platforms influence consumer responses to online marketing. The study highlights that digital marketing influences financial decision-making by increasing product awareness and shaping consumer confidence, expectations, and perceptions of financial institutions. It also demonstrates the need to balance digital convenience with careful evaluation of financial information. However, its effectiveness depends on transparency, information accuracy, financial literacy, and source credibility. The paper emphasises responsible marketing practices that prioritise consumer interests alongside business objectives. It

latest.title: Algorithmic Gatekeepers in the Generative AI Era: Platform Asymmetry in AI-Mediated Business Visibility
latest.abstract: The rapid proliferation of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) is fundamentally reshaping digital intermediation.Unlike traditional search engines that rank hyperlinks, generative AI agents synthesize and directly endorse commercial entities, acting as novel algorithmic gatekeepers.However, the structural dynamics of this AI-mediated commercial visibility remain largely unexamined.This study investigates platform asymmetry, industry specialization, and geographical consistency in AI business recommendations.Utilizing the AI Visibility Index, we analyze 79,077 businesslevel observations across 44 industries and 20 countries, auditing the zero-shot recommendation behaviors of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok.Our findings reveal profound structural asymmetry and severe crossplatform fragmentation.Gemini emerges as the dominant intermediary, capturing approximately 50% of the normalized visibility share and leading in 35 of 44 industries, particularly in local and consumer-facing services.Conversely, Claude demonstrates distinct specialization, dominating nine highly regulated, B2B, and financial sectors.Furthermore, we identify severe epistemic fragmentation, with only 261 businesslocation category combinations achieving visibility across all four platforms.These findings challenge foundational marketing paradigms, notably Keller's Customer-Based Brand Equity framework, by demonstrating that brand salience is now strictly contingent upon "algorithmic access."We discuss the imperative for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), the strategic necessity of platform specific visibility management, and the urgent need for regulatory frameworks to address the opaque market shaping power of agentic AI gatekeepers.

latest.title: Parental information, motivation, and self-efficacy in toddler skincare brand preference: an Information–Motivation–Behavioural Skills framework
latest.abstract: Introduction Growing awareness of toddler well-being and the availability of specialized skincare products have increased parental attention to skincare choices. This study examines the relationships of parental knowledge, brand awareness, parental attitude, perceived social norms, and perceived effectiveness with skincare brand preference, while investigating the mediating role of self-efficacy within the Information–Motivation–Behavioural Skills (IMB) framework. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 126 parents recruited through convenience sampling. Data were collected using a structured Google Forms questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model was assessed for reliability and validity, while the structural model was evaluated using path coefficients, bootstrapping, and the coefficient of determination (R 2). Results Parental knowledge, brand awareness, parental attitude, and perceived social norms did not show statistically significant direct relationships with skincare brand preference. Perceived effectiveness demonstrated a significant positive relationship with skincare brand preference (β = 0.576, p = 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed significant indirect through self-efficacy for parental attitude (β = 0.083, p = 0.031) and perceived effectiveness (β = 0.208, p = 0.001). The indirect relationships involving parental knowledge, brand awareness, and perceived social norms were not statistically significant. Discussion The findings highlight the relevance of perceived product effectiveness and self-efficacy in understanding parental skincare brand preferences. latest.title: Human appearance preferences as emergent properties of generalised learning
latest.abstract: The tendency to find some individuals or personal features more visually or aesthetically appealing than others (appearance preferences) is a widespread human experience. The underlying causes of why some people or features in particular are considered attractive has been variably conceptualised as being the product of cultural power structures, a by-product of broader cognitive processes, and a reflection of 'innate' appearance preferences and processes shaped by sexual selection. Evolutionary-adaptationist and cognitive processing perspectives both prompted the development of a large literature attempting to understand why some specific traits are considered attractive. More recently, however, questions have emerged regarding the validity of the proposed 'adaptive' benefits of some of these traits within an evolutionary framework. Simultaneously, cross-cultural research has demonstrated that while some underlying cognitive processes may be similar across populations, specific appearance preferences are more variable than some 'functional' adaptationist hypotheses predict. The current paper outlines what key challenges exist for an approach to appearance preferences that focuses on specific functional mating adaptations, and how cognitive and cultural processes may provide a more robust explanation of current cross- and intra-cultural data without a requirement for sexual selection to have played a role. It then argues that a large portion of human appearance preferences - including those previously thought to be human universals - may in fact be a by-product of broader perceptual and learning processes interacting with cultural-evolutionary feedback. latest.title: Peran Self-Control Dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Lifestyle dan User Experience Terhadap Impulsive Buying Pada Generasi Z Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee is influenced by lifestyle and user experience; however, previous findings are inconsistent, and the role of self-control as a moderator has not been tested together with both factors. This study aims to analyze the role of self-control in moderating the effects of lifestyle and user experience on impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee. The study employs an associative-causal quantitative approach with purposive sampling of 100 active Generation Z Shopee users. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by ANOVA (F-test) to examine the simultaneous effects. The results show that lifestyle and user experience have positive and significant effects on impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously together with self-control and its two interactions (F = 12.325; p < 0.001). Self-control has a negative and significant effect and negatively and significantly moderates the effects of lifestyle and user experience, thereby weakening both relationships. The novelty of this study lies in its integrated model, which simultaneously examines lifestyle and user experience with self-control as a moderator. The better Generation Z's self-control, the lower the tendency toward impulsive buying, even when influenced by lifestyle and an engaging online shopping experience. These findings are expected to provide insights for consumers and e-commerce platform managers in understanding and managing purchasing behavior.

latest.title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
latest.abstract: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

latest.title: The 7P Marketing Mix and Repurchase Intention in Online Footwear Shopping: The Effect of Utilitarian and Hedonic Value
latest.abstract: Encouraging customers to buy again remains a challenge for footwear brands in e-commerce. This study examines how the 7P marketing mix elements relate to utilitarian and hedonic value and how these values relate to repurchase intention. Guided by the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, survey data from 247 female consumers of Malcca who purchased through Shopee or TikTok Shop were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Product, price, and physical evidence were positively associated with utilitarian value, whereas product, promotion, people, and physical evidence were positively associated with hedonic value. Place and process showed no significant relationships with either value dimension. Both values positively influenced repurchase intention, with a larger estimated coefficient for utilitarian value. Significant indirect relationships were identified for product, price, and physical evidence through utilitarian value, and for people and physical evidence through hedonic value. Physical evidence was the only marketing mix element with significant indirect relationships through both value dimensions. These findings suggest that footwear brands should prioritize price–quality alignment, accurate product information, and effective visual presentation to strengthen functional and experiential value. The study extends the S-O-R framework by illustrating distinct value pathways associated with repurchase intention.

latest.title: Creating an Educational Blue Ocean: Value Innovation and Sustainable Ecosystem Transformation
latest.abstract: Competitive pressures can encourage educational institutions to imitate established practices, making it harder to offer distinctive learning experiences that respond to changing educational and societal needs. This study developed a conceptual pathway for applying Blue Ocean Strategy in education by examining value innovation, institutional differentiation, and educational ecosystem transformation. Using a qualitative integrative literature review and conceptual analysis, the study synthesized scholarship on Blue Ocean Strategy, educational competition, value creation, and institutional transformation. The synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions. Strategic repositioning directs institutional priorities toward differentiation and efficient resource use. Redefining educational value emphasizes distinctive learning experiences, stakeholder participation, and contributions to society. The Eliminate–Reduce–Raise–Create framework translates value innovation into practice by eliminating activities of limited educational value, reducing operational inefficiencies, raising educational quality and institutional accountability, and creating new learning opportunities and collaborative services. Sustaining educational value requires collaboration among students, educators, families, government agencies, industry, and communities. The proposed Educational Blue Ocean pathway connects these dimensions and offers a conceptual basis for understanding how institutions can develop distinctive, adaptive, inclusive, and sustainable educational environments.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kredibilitas Affiliate Marketing dan Kepercayaan Konsumen terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk di TikTok Shop
latest.venue: Best Journal of Administration and Management
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of affiliate marketing credibility and consumer trust on purchase decisions for products on TikTok Shop, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative explanatory design was employed. The population comprised TikTok Shop users who had purchased products through affiliate content, and 350 respondents were selected by purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire with 15 five-point Likert items measuring affiliate marketing credibility (expertise, honesty, communicator attractiveness, information credibility, and consistency), consumer trust (seller integrity, transaction reliability, transaction security, product conformity, and promise fulfilment), and purchase decision (product, brand, seller, timing, and quantity choice). All items were valid (corrected item-total r = 0.604–0.724) and reliable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.836–0.861), and the classical assumptions were met. Multiple linear regression showed that affiliate marketing credibility had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (B = 0.434; t = 9.542; p < 0.001), as did consumer trust (B = 0.273; t = 5.575; p < 0.001). Simultaneously, both variables significantly affected purchase decisions (F = 82.239; p < 0.001) and explained 32.2% of its variance. Affiliate credibility was the dominant predictor (beta = 0.439). Sellers and brands should therefore recruit knowledgeable and honest affiliates while strengthening transaction security and product conformity to convert affiliate exposure into purchases.

latest.title: Hubungan antara Persepsi Harga dan Kepuasan Penggunaan Layanan Netflix dengan Minat Berlangganan Ulang pada Mahasiswa di Semarang
latest.abstract: The increasing use of video streaming services among college students and intensifying digital competition drive users to evaluate price perception and user satisfaction before resubscribing. This study aims to analyze the relationship between price perception, user satisfaction, and resubscription intention for Netflix services among college students in Semarang. This quantitative survey research involved 100 active university students in Semarang, selected through cluster sampling and purposive sampling techniques. Data were gathered via a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using validity, reliability, classical assumption tests, Pearson Product Moment correlation, and multiple correlation using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. The results indicate that price perception has a positive and significant relationship with resubscription intention (r = 0.586; p < 0.001). User satisfaction also demonstrates a positive and significant relationship with resubscription intention (r = 0.546; p < 0.001). Simultaneously, price perception and user satisfaction have a positive and significant relationship with resubscription intention (R = 0.654; R² = 0.428; p < 0.001). Together, these variables account for 42.8% of the variance in resubscription intention, while the remaining 57.2% is explained by external factors. These findings support the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) Theory, illustrating how price perception and satisfaction act as stimuli processed internally to form a resubscription response.

latest.title: Group, Individual and Cultural Determinants of Consumer Decision-Making and Their Implications for Marketing Strategy in Nigeria
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examined the group, individual and cultural determinants of consumer decision-making and their implications for marketing strategy in Nigeria, where consumer behaviour is complex, shaped by cultural diversity, collectivist values and rapidly changing digital markets, yet existing research often examines group, individual and cultural determinants in isolation, leaving marketers without an integrated framework. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and using a multi-stage sampling technique comprising stratified, cluster and systematic random sampling, data were collected from 304 adult consumers across the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria — North-Central 51, North-East 50, North-West 51, South-East 50, South-South 51 and South-West 51 — using a structured questionnaire, and data were analysed with SPSS 27.0 and AMOS 26.0 using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression and Structural Equation Modelling. Results showed that all determinants significantly influence consumer decision-making, with Reference Group emerging as the strongest predictor (β = 0.338, p = 0.000), followed by Culture (β = 0.271), Individual Determinants (β = 0.249), Sub-Culture (β = 0.182) and Social Class (β = 0.148), and jointly the predictors explained 61.2% of variation in decision-making (R² = 0.612, F (5, 298) = 94.021, p = 0.000), while the decision process significantly mediated the relationship between determinants and marketing strategy (indirect effect = 0.412, p = 0.000) and all six hypotheses were accepted. The study concludes that Nigerian consumer decision-making is socially and culturally embedded, and marketers should leverage reference groups, localise strategy by culture and zone, build trust through transparency and support c

latest.title: Development of Brand Communication for Pla Meng in Surat Thani Province
latest.venue: Journal of Multidisciplinary in Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study aimed to (1) examine the local identity of Pla Meng (Stinging Catfish) in Surat Thani, (2) develop brand communication guidelines for Pla Meng, and (3) evaluate the effectiveness of these guidelines. The research was grounded in theories of marketing communication, communication development, brand identity, and related empirical studies. A mixed-methods design was employed. The qualitative phase involved documentary research, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and non-participant observation, engaging a total of 54 key informants. The quantitative phase consisted of a questionnaire survey administered to 400 respondents, comprising local residents and tourists in Surat Thani. The findings indicate that the identity of Pla Meng is defined by its status as a native freshwater species of Surat Thani, distinguished by its firm, fibrous flesh, low fat content, and non-mushy texture, as well as its traditional processing methods based on local wisdom. The proposed brand communication guidelines consist of five components: fish farming, smoked Pla Meng production, product processing, menu innovation, and market distribution, with information disseminated primarily through social media platforms. Hypothesis testing indicated that personal variables, such as age, education, occupation, income, and place of residence, significantly influence levels of brand awareness of Pla Meng through digital marketing communication. Overall brand awareness remains relatively low; however, a strong positive correlation was found between brand awareness and consumer perceptions of the Pla Meng brand. The study proposes communication strategies that foreground local identity and cultural value to strengthen brand positioning and enhance the capacity of community-based entrep

latest.title: Bridging Quality to Buying Action: The Mediating Mechanism of Price Perception in Consumer Footwear Purchases
latest.abstract: This study aims to investigate the direct effects of product quality and price on purchase decisions among footwear consumers in Bandung, while examining the mediating role of price in bridging product quality to actual buying decisions. Employing a quantitative explanatory survey design, this research gathered empirical data from 100 consumers who purchased specific brand shoes in Bandung via purposive sampling. The data were evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), encompassing convergent and discriminant validity, reliability assessments, structural path bootstrapping, as well as predictive metrics including PLSpredict and CVPAT. The measurement model confirmed robust convergent validity, discriminant validity, and composite reliability without multicollinearity issues. The structural assessment revealed that product quality significantly drives price perception (beta = 0.851), while both product quality (beta = 0.487) and price (beta = 0.480) positively determine purchase decisions (R2 = 86.6%). Crucially, price acts as a significant complementary partial mediator (beta = 0.409, p < 0.001), with strong out-of-sample predictive capability confirmed by PLSpredict (Q2predict > 0.70) and negative CVPAT average loss differences. Theoretically, these results enrich consumer behavior literature by validating price as an active value-transmitting mediator rather than merely a monetary sacrifice. Practically, footwear marketers must prioritize core material craftsmanship and adopt value-based pricing strategies, ensuring marketing communications transparently articulate functional superiority to justify the price point and stimulate purchases. latest.title: Designing competitive generative AI services: Consumer preferences and pricing implications for SMEs and venture companies
latest.abstract: This study examines consumer preferences for generative AI (GenAI) services and explores how these preferences influence willingness to pay (WTP) and market competitiveness, with a particular focus on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and venture companies. As GenAI technologies rapidly evolve and the application service market expands, understanding how consumers evaluate different service attributes becomes critical for designing competitive and sustainable business models. This study employs a conjoint analysis combined with a mixed logit model to capture consumer heterogeneity and analyze trade-offs among key service attributes. Six attributes are considered: purpose of use, data accuracy and timeliness, disclosure of data sources, data bias and personal information verification, type of service provider, and service fees. The results indicate that consumers place the greatest importance on service fees, followed by trust-related attributes such as data accuracy, verification, and transparency. In addition, the findings reveal no statistically significant preference for large global or domestic firms, while SMEs and venture companies are positively and significantly preferred, suggesting that competitive advantage in the GenAI application market may depend more on service design than on firm size. These findings contribute to the literature by providing an integrated analysis of consumer preference structures and pricing in the GenAI service market. From a practical perspective, the study offers strategic insights for SMEs and venture companies, emphasizing the importance of trust-enhancing features and value-based pricing strategies in achieving sustainable competitiveness.

latest.title: Driving Private University Choice: A Combined PLS-SEM, IPMA, and NCA Analysis of Brand Image and Trust
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Brand Image and Trust drive prospective students’ private university choices in Bandung. We examine both direct structural relationships and the necessary prerequisite conditions required to optimize institutional enrollment. To conduct this investigation, the authors surveyed 100 university students using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. This study subsequently analyzed the quantitative data utilizing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS to assess path relationships and predictive power. Finally, the analytical framework integrated Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) to identify operational priorities and critical bottleneck thresholds. The PLS-SEM path analysis confirms that Brand Image directly drives Student Choice (β = 0.411) and significantly mediates the impact of Trust (β = 0.325), while Trust serves as the primary predictor of Brand Image (β = 0.790, R2 = 0.572). IPMA identifies Trust—specifically Benevolence and Integrity—as the highest-leverage area for institutional improvement due to its high overall importance (0.713) but lower current performance (50.500). Furthermore, NCA reveals that Brand Benefits (d = 0.526) and Benevolence (d = 0.428) act as indispensable necessary conditions, establishing that achieving top-tier enrollment outcomes (90%–100%) requires high minimum bottleneck capacities in Brand (68%) and Trust (73%). Implications for institutional management, must allocate resources strategically by first satisfying essential bottleneck conditions. Institutions should guarantee clear Brand Benefits and show institutional Benevolence to avoid enrollment barriers, while enhancing Integrity to build long-term brand equity and secure stu

latest.title: Consumer response to a multi-channel promotional campaign for local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq: a mixed-methods evaluation
latest.abstract: Introduction This study looked at how a multi-channel promotional campaign, affected what people know, how they feel, and whether they actually bought local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methods A single cohort of 400 consumers was surveyed before the campaign (September–October 2025) and re-contacted after campaign implementation (July–August 2026). After matching respondents, we were able to compare 165 individuals with confidence. Our questionnaire covered knowledge, attitudes, buying habits, campaign exposure and recognition (distinguishing visibility, engagement, and message recall), message quality, barriers to purchase, and willingness to pay. We used a mix of statistical tools, from simple comparisons to more advanced techniques like regression analysis and clustering. Results Knowledge increased significantly from pre-campaign (2.621 ± 0.904) to post-campaign (2.903 ± 0.992; Δ = +0.282, p = 0.003, Cohen’s dz. = 0.236). No statistically significant overall changes were detected in attitudes (Δ = +0.074, p = 0.328) or purchasing behavior (Δ = −0.012, p = 0.872). Overall campaign exposure was moderate (2.653/5), with social media exposure higher than traditional media. Barriers to purchasing included insufficient label information (3.313), difficulty finding the product (3.275), and weak packaging/branding (3.258). PCA identified eight underlying dimensions explaining 63.3% of variance, and K-means clustering produced five exploratory consumer profiles: “Informed but barrier-constrained engaged consumers” (21.0%); “Low-engagement/low-response consumers” (17.0%); “Committed local-olive-oil advocates” (29.5%); “Under-reached but potentially receptive consumers” (8.2%); and “Positive but underinformed consumers” (24.2%). latest.title: The Effect of Customer Experience on Purchase Intention in Indonesian E-Commerce: Mediating Effect of Brand Trust
latest.abstract: Rapid digitalization has intensified e-commerce competition in Indonesia, highlighting the importance of customer experience and brand trust in shaping consumers’ purchase intentions. This study examines whether brand trust mediates the relationship between customer experience and purchase intention among Indonesian e-commerce users. Drawing on Stimulus–Organism–Response theory and relationship marketing theory, the study conceptualizes customer experience as the stimulus, brand trust as the psychological mechanism, and purchase intention as the behavioral response. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 280 active e-commerce users who had made at least one online purchase during the previous six months. Data were collected using a structured five-point Likert questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that customer experience has a positive and significant relationship with purchase intention, customer experience positively relates to brand trust, and brand trust positively relates to purchase intention. The indirect effect indicates partial mediation. The findings suggest that positive digital experiences can strengthen trust, which in turn is associated with stronger purchase intentions. The study contributes context-specific evidence from Indonesian e-commerce and clarifies the process through which experience is linked to purchase intention.

latest.title: Economía de la atención y decisiones de consumo (2020–2026): una revisión sistemática según PRISMA
latest.abstract: The attention economy has become an important topic because it seeks to understand how consumer behavior is determined in this era of the vast digital environment, where attention has become a crucial and relevant factor in purchasing decisions. Therefore, the objective of our systematic review was to analyze the scientific evidence on the impact of the attention economy on consumer decisions between 2020 and 2026. The study was designed according to the PRISMA guidelines, reviewing studies indexed in databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SciELO, and Google Scholar. The results show that strategies such as personalized advertising, visual attention, and recommendation algorithms increase purchase intention, brand preference, and consumer loyalty. Issues such as ethics in consumer decision-making, the use of digital technology, and cognitive overload were also identified. Concluding that the attention economy is a determining factor in consumption decisions and is a strategic element for planning digital marketing activities in various organizations, emphasizing the need to promote responsible practices that balance both business efficiency and consumer well-being.

latest.title: Links Between Environmental Knowledge, Environmental Attitudes, and the Green Purchasing Behavior of Young-Aged Muslims in Sri Lanka
latest.abstract: Due to growing environmental awareness and the increased understanding of the impact of unsustainable consumption patterns on the planet, modern-day consumers are showing greater sensitivity towards green products when making purchasing decisions. This growing demand for environmentally friendly products and services has induced many firms to increasingly adopt green marketing as a strategy to gain a competitive advantage. Nevertheless, the younger generation seems to have different attitudes and beliefs, and this has made them critically evaluate their choices related to green products. For the past few decades, environmental hazards and greater concerns towards environmental sustainability have made green purchasing a significant focus of numerous studies. However, a vital area, i.e., the religious values and the green purchasing behaviors of the young-aged population in Sri Lanka, seems understudied. Thus, the main objective of this research is to empirically examine the influence of environmental knowledge and environmental attitudes on the green purchasing behavior of young-aged Muslims in Sri Lanka. This study is a survey-based, cross-sectional, quantitative study, and the SPSS Statistics 26.0 software package is relied upon in analyzing the data. The data for the study were gathered through a self-administered questionnaire from 384 respondents covering all provinces of the country. The findings reveal that both environmental knowledge and environmental attitudes play a significant role in determining the green purchasing behavior of this faith community. Moreover, environmental knowledge positively influences the green purchasing behavior of this group more extensively than environmental attitudes. This understanding of the green purchasing behavior of young-age

latest.title: AI-Mediated Care-Washing: Discourse, Cognition, and Dual-Layer Decoupling in China’s Elderly Companion Product Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study examines how enterprises in China’s AI companion product sector publicly construct their products as legitimate care solutions for elderly users, and whether practitioners privately understand that discourse’s relationship to commercial and technical realities. A two-phase sequential qualitative design was employed. Study 1 conducted qualitative content analysis of twelve enterprise-affiliated texts through hybrid deductive-inductive coding; Study 2 conducted semi-structured interviews with eight practitioners in mainland China and Hong Kong, analyzed through thematic analysis. Study 1 identified two discourse patterns: emotional equivalence claims constructing AI interaction as equivalent to human companionship, and vulnerability erasure replacing elderly vulnerability with technological empowerment. Study 2 found that practitioners acknowledged a gap between promotional claims and technical capability, maintained different communicative registers for internal and external audiences, and were privately aware of the vulnerability enterprise discourse suppresses. This study proposes AI-mediated care-washing as a dual-layer decoupling construct extending care-washing theory, contributes to institutional decoupling theory by documenting communicative register bifurcation, and advances vulnerable consumer research by identifying filial obligation as the mechanism converting elderly vulnerability into purchasing behaviour.

latest.title: The Role of Images in Online Customer Reviews: Evidence from Trendyol
latest.venue: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study conducts a qualitative analysis aimed at understanding the use of image in customer reviews on Trendyol, one of the most preferred e-commerce platforms in Turkey. The purpose of this research is to determine the function of image-based customer reviews on online shopping platforms in conveying consumer experience and to examine how these reviews constitute a source of information for potential consumers. The product appearing first under Trendyol's "Most Rated" sorting option in the "shoes" category was selected, and its image-based customer reviews were examined using qualitative content analysis. The 282 image-based reviews made during the six-month period were analysed using MAXQDA 24 software. During the analysis process, both image-based and written content were coded, revealing how the images interacted with textual expressions, and key themes were identified. The findings show that images serve as a reinforcing element of satisfaction in particularly high-rated and positive reviews, while acting as a corroborating factor for dissatisfaction in low-rated and negative reviews. It has been determined that product images are dominant, while usage and defective product images are used to detail the experience. Interpreted through Dual Coding Theory, these findings suggest that visual and verbal elements can complement each other in communicating consumer experiences. Overall, the study highlights the role of image-based customer reviews in conveying product-related information to prospective consumers.

latest.title: AiWOM vs. influencer eWOM: an SOR perspective on source credibility and purchase intention
latest.abstract: Introduction The growth of artificial intelligence in marketing has introduced AI-generated word of mouth (AiWOM) alongside influencer eWOM (IeWOM). Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework and Source Credibility Theory (SCT), this study compares the effects of AiWOM and IeWOM on purchase intention (PI) and examines the mediating role of source credibility. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with a verified sample of 562 active digital consumers aged 18 to 45 in Palestine, recruited through a combination of purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4, and the differences between the two sources were tested with bootstrapped paired-difference tests. Results Both human influencers and AI sources positively affected source credibility, but human influencers exerted a statistically significantly stronger effect on source credibility and purchase intention. Source credibility functioned as a complementary partial mediator for both IeWOM and AiWOM, with significant indirect effects coexisting with significant direct effects. Discussion Human influencers remain the more persuasive force in digital marketing, although AiWOM represents a viable emerging channel. By providing a formal, same-sample statistical comparison of human and AI eWOM within an integrated SOR-SCT model in an under-researched collectivist market, the study suggests that marketers should anchor credibility-building in human influencers while deploying AiWOM as a complementary, scalable channel.

latest.title: Impact of service value fluctuation on market share: a simulation study
latest.abstract: Service value is a critical factor for gaining market share and retaining customers. Although the importance of service value is well-established, it is often challenging to consistently provide high-value service owing to various factors, such as human error and unforeseen incidents. Therefore, understanding the influence of service value fluctuations on market share is crucial for service providers to develop effective strategies. To evaluate this influence, we propose a consumer decision model that considers past service-use experiences and word-of-mouth. Moreover, consumers’ selection results influence other consumers’ choices through information diffusion. We investigate the model behavior through analytical analysis and simulation, and the results demonstrate that the model can reproduce insights from previous studies. Additionally, we evaluated the influence of service value fluctuation on market share across several market characteristics, particularly service-use frequency and the ease of word-of-mouth dissemination. The results revealed that fluctuations negatively impact market share, even if they increase the value received by consumers. Moreover, in markets characterized by high service-use frequency, the results imply that marketing strategies focused on providing information to consumers are replaced less effective. In such markets, service value fluctuation is critical for gaining market share.

latest.title: Social Media Influencer Marketing Tools and Consumer Purchase Behaviour of Undergraduate Students in the University of Benin
latest.abstract: This study examined the relationship between social media influencer marketing tools and the consumer purchase behaviour of students at the University of Benin, focusing on Facebook, Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), and YouTube. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 395 undergraduate and postgraduate students selected using Yamane’s formula. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation, t-test, ANOVA, and multiple regression with SPSS version 20.0. The findings revealed that all four social media platforms have positive and statistically significant relationships with consumer purchase behaviour. Correlation analysis showed significant associations between purchase intention and Facebook, Instagram, X, and YouTube, with YouTube and Instagram demonstrating stronger relationships. Regression results indicated that the four platforms jointly explained 58.4% of the variation in purchase intention, with YouTube emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by Instagram, Facebook, and X. The model also showed no multicollinearity concerns. Demographic factors were also found to significantly influence purchase behaviour. Gender showed a significant difference in purchasing patterns, with female students recording slightly higher mean scores. Educational qualification and age also significantly affected consumer purchase behaviour. The study concludes that social media influencer marketing significantly shapes students’ purchase decisions, particularly through visually engaging platforms such as YouTube and Instagram. It recommends that businesses strategically use credible and engaging influencer content while considering demographic differences. The study contributes emp

latest.title: The recommender–context fit: AI versus human advice, trust, and purchase intentions in service decisions
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services

latest.title: Influence of Visual Merchandising on Fashion Oriented Impulse Buying Behavior of Women in Kurunegala District
latest.abstract: This study investigates the influence of visual merchandising on fashion-oriented impulse buying behavior among women in Kurunegala District, Sri Lanka. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how visual merchandising elements affect consumer purchasing decisions in the post-pandemic retail environment, where shopping patterns have evolved significantly. The study employed a quantitative research approach using a structured online survey methodology. Data were collected from 384 women consumers aged 25 and above through convenience sampling. The research framework was grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response model, examining four key visual merchandising dimensions: window display, lighting, store layout, and promotional signage as predictors of impulse buying behavior. Primary data collection was conducted through social media platforms using a validated questionnaire with 5-point Likert scale measurements. Multiple regression analysis was utilized to examine relationships between visual merchandising elements and the impulse buying behavior. Data reliability and validity were ensured through Cronbach's alpha testing and Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) analysis. The research findings reveal significant relationships between visual merchandising elements and women's impulse buying behavior in the fashion retail context. The study contributes valuable insights by identifying which visual merchandising strategies most effectively influence consumer behavior in the Sri Lankan market, providing practical implications for retailers seeking to optimize their strategies to enhance customer engagement and increase sales performance.

latest.title: The Effect of Affiliate Content and Brand Awareness on Purchase Decisions on TikTok
latest.abstract: The growth of social commerce has made TikTok a channel for product promotion, particularly through affiliate content that combines recommendations with direct purchase links. However, purchasing decisions may also depend on consumers’ ability to recognize and recall promoted brands. This study examines the partial and simultaneous effects of affiliate content and brand awareness on purchasing decisions among students. A quantitative survey was conducted from June to September 2026 involving 96 students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS. The results show that affiliate content has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions (B = 0.217, p = 0.004), while brand awareness also has a positive and significant effect (B = 0.615, p < 0.001). Brand awareness shows a stronger association, with a standardized beta of 0.681 compared with 0.209 for affiliate content. The regression model is significant (F = 86.386, p < 0.001) and explains 65.0% of the variance in purchasing decisions. These findings suggest that businesses should prioritize consistent brand-building strategies while supporting them with informative, credible, and engaging affiliate content to strengthen consumer purchasing decisions in TikTok social commerce.

latest.title: Social media marketing and tourism purchase intention: Bibliometric S–O–R synthesis and workforce implications
latest.abstract: Social media marketing can shape tourism purchase decisions through traveller-generated information, influencer communication, and interactions with service providers, although these sources do not necessarily generate the same form of trust. This study integrates bibliometric analysis of 162 Web of Science articles published during 2015–2024 with a theory-driven stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework. A structured selection process reduced 286 identified records to 162 eligible articles after duplicate removal, title-and-abstract screening, and in-depth eligibility assessment. The corpus covers 534 authors and 93 journal titles. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified 477 distinct terms; applying a minimum occurrence threshold of five retained 35 keywords, organized into four clusters with 142 links and a total link strength of 326. The conceptual synthesis differentiates perceived user-generated content quality, influencer credibility, and provider interactivity as stimuli; provider trust and customer engagement as organism-level states; and intention to purchase a specified tourism service as the response. Eight theoretical propositions articulate direct and indirect relationships, including boundary conditions concerning review valence and the relevance of an endorsement to the provider. Implications for human resource management focus on frontline digital communication competence, service knowledge, responsible empowerment, and cross-functional coordination. Bibliometric network patterns describe the structure of scholarship, whereas the proposed behavioral pathways are developed theoretically and remain hypotheses for subsequent empirical testing.

latest.title: Corporate Social Responsibility Communication in Luxury Fashion on X: A Computational Content Analysis of How Framing Relates to Audience Engagement
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: Luxury fashion brands increasingly adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices amid regulatory pressures, yet communicating these practices remains challenging. Using computational content analysis and regression modeling, this research analyzed 259,200 English posts by luxury fashion brands on X to examine how message valence (positive vs. negative tone) and CSR theme (environmental vs. social) relate to audience engagement (likes/reposts/replies). Results showed that CSR content accounted for up to 1.2% of these brands' annual posts and was mostly positive in tone and environmental in focus. While neither message valence nor CSR theme alone predicted audience engagement, CSR theme interacted significantly with brand value tier (high vs. low). For low‐tier brands, social (vs. environmental) CSR theme drew fewer likes and reposts, whereas such patterns were not observed among high‐tier brands. These findings advance CSR communication research and offer luxury fashion brands managerial insights into tailoring CSR framing strategies to their brand value tier.

latest.title: Antropomorfización de agentes de inteligencia artificial generativa y arrepentimiento poscompra en consumidores de Quevedo: el papel del locus de control y del tipo de compra
latest.abstract: La incorporación de rasgos humanos en asistentes comerciales puede modificar la responsabilidad que los consumidores atribuyen a sus decisiones. El objetivo fue analizar la relación entre antropomorfización del agente y arrepentimiento poscompra, considerando el locus de control percibido en la decisión como mediador y el tipo de compra como moderador. Se utilizó un diseño factorial 2 × 2 entre sujetos con 200 consumidores de Quevedo, distribuidos en cuatro condiciones de 50 participantes. Las viñetas combinaron antropomorfización baja o alta con una finalidad utilitaria o hedónica de compra. Se mantuvieron constantes el producto, el precio y el desenlace desfavorable. Se estimó un ANOVA factorial y un sistema de regresiones con moderación de la trayectoria entre el mediador y el resultado, correspondiente al Modelo 14 de PROCESS. Los intervalos de los efectos indirectos se obtuvieron mediante 5.000 remuestreos bootstrap percentiles. La antropomorfización se relacionó positivamente con la atribución externa de control (b = 0,712). El efecto indirecto fue negativo en la compra utilitaria (-0,417) y positivo en la hedónica (0,373). El índice de mediación moderada fue 0,790, con un intervalo que excluyó el cero. El patrón indicó que la relación entre control atribuido al agente y arrepentimiento dependió de la finalidad de compra. Su interpretación se circunscribió a respuestas ante viñetas y no permitió establecer mecanismos emocionales adicionales ni desempeño comercial efectivo.

latest.title: Assessing the Informational Value of Sustainable Packaging Under Information Overload: A Decision‐Support Perspective
latest.abstract: Packaging plays a strategic role in sustainability communication under information overload conditions, yet the informational value of sustainable packaging is rarely assessed from a decision‐orientated perspective. This study proposes and empirically tests a decision‐support framework that integrates expert‐defined sustainability ideals with consumer perception gaps under uncertainty. Using fermented dairy products as an empirical context, the research combines focus group evaluations, semantic differential scales and intuitionistic fuzzy modelling to examine how sustainable packaging information is processed in real‐world decision settings. The results indicate that the informational value does not stem from the volume of sustainability‐related messages, but rather from their coherence, hierarchical organisation and alignment with functional and visual decision heuristics. Functional attributes, such as ease of use and ergonomics, show the strongest alignment with expert expectations, whereas sustainability cues generate informational value only when embedded in concrete usage contexts and supported by clear visual signals. The proposed framework offers strategic guidance for sustainable packaging design and sustainability communication under constrained consumer attention.

latest.title: Digital Media Influence on Consumer Decision-Making: An Empirical Study with Special Reference to Tourism Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Global Research Innovations & Technology (IJGRIT).
latest.abstract: With an emphasis on the functions of social media advertising, behavioral intentions, visitor happiness, and information provided by other travelers, this study investigates the impact of digital media on travel destination decision-making among tourists. The research, which is based on the Uses and Gratification (U&G) theory, suggests that travelers actively use digital platforms to meet particular social and informational requirements, which in turn influence their destination selections. Using a standardized questionnaire, 178 respondents provided primary data, which was then analyzed using multiple linear regression, reliability analysis, and descriptive statistics. The Shapiro-Wilk test verified a non-normal, negatively skewed distribution typical of high-agreement satisfaction surveys, and the measurement scale showed great internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.959). 54.8% of the variance in the outcome variable was explained by the regression model (R = 0.740, R² = 0.548, Adjusted R² = 0.477). Three of the four hypothesized relationships social media advertising, behavioral intentions, and visitor satisfaction were found to have a statistically significant positive impact on travelers' decisions about destinations, while the impact of information from other travelers was not. These findings have practical implications for destination marketers and tourism service providers looking to maximize digital engagement strategies, as they indicate that curated advertising content, travelers' behavioral predispositions, and satisfaction levels are more significant influences on destination choice than peer-generated information alone.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Transformasi Ekonomi Digital dan Evolusi Pola Konsumsi: Tinjauan Literatur tentang Perubahan Perilaku Belanja di Era Internet
hot.abstract: Transformasi ekonomi digital telah mengubah pola konsumsi masyarakat secara fundamental, terutama dengan meningkatnya penggunaan e-commerce, layanan berbasis sharing economy, serta metode pembayaran digital yang semakin mempermudah transaksi. Penelitian ini merupakan tinjauan pustaka dengan pendekatan kualitatif dan analisis deskriptif yang bertujuan untuk mengkaji perubahan perilaku belanja di era internet. Data penelitian diambil dari Google Scholar untuk periode 2015–2025, dengan total 50 artikel yang diseleksi menjadi 24 artikel yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa digitalisasi telah mendorong pergeseran preferensi konsumen dari belanja konvensional ke belanja daring, dengan faktor utama seperti kenyamanan, efisiensi, dan personalisasi layanan. Media sosial dan pemasaran berbasis influencer memainkan peran penting dalam keputusan pembelian, sementara model bisnis baru seperti cloud kitchen dan layanan pesan-antar semakin mengubah pola konsumsi, terutama di industri makanan dan minuman. Namun, fenomena ini juga menghadirkan tantangan, termasuk peningkatan belanja impulsif, risiko keamanan data, dan dampak negatif terhadap sektor ritel tradisional. Implikasi dari penelitian ini menyoroti pentingnya adaptasi bisnis terhadap tren digital, perlunya regulasi yang lebih kuat untuk melindungi konsumen, serta peningkatan literasi digital dan keuangan bagi masyarakat. Penelitian ini memiliki keterbatasan dalam cakupan data sekunder dan tidak menggali aspek demografis atau budaya yang dapat memengaruhi adopsi digitalisasi. Oleh karena itu, studi lanjutan dengan pendekatan empiris diperlukan untuk memperoleh pemahaman yang lebih mendalam mengenai transformasi konsumsi di era digital.

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance.
