latest.title: Building socially responsible global brand identity with AI and sustainability strategy
latest.abstract: Purpose This research is an attempt to systematically review the current body of literature about strategic use of artificial intelligence and sustainability orientation to build a responsible global identity. Design/methodology/approach To conduct a systematic review and present a qualitative synthesis of literature, this research uses a multi-faceted four-stage PRISMA protocol that includes identification, screening, eligibility and inclusion. Findings Our analysis of academic knowledge reveals that available brand strategy literature mainly considers the consumer perspective and does not include the perspective of the global community of stakeholders. To address this gap, this study integrates sustainability orientation and AI strategy with governance, brand resilience and standardization–adaptation theory to explain how organizations can build socially responsible global brand identities. In doing so, the study provides a novel framework for balancing global consistency and local relevance in increasingly transparent and digitally connected markets. Originality/value This research offers a comprehensive analysis of theoretical, methodological and empirical knowledge to find answers to the research questions raised by the current context of sustainability consciousness and new age of artificial technologies.

latest.title: Metaverse-enabled logistics: a digital twin for human-centric supply chains
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how Metaverse technologies – such as digital twins, artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain and immersive interfaces – can support supply chain resilience by improving information flows, disruption detection and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach Based on a structured conceptual synthesis of literature on supply chain resilience and advanced digital technologies, the study proposes a five-stage framework for Metaverse-enabled resilience assessment and illustrates its application through an automotive component supply disruption scenario. The stages include identifying key supply chain components, assessing risks, simulating response strategies, applying immersive training and supporting continuous improvement. Each stage integrates specific technological functions such as digital twin modeling, AI-driven analytics, augmented reality and virtual reality (AR–VR) simulations and blockchain-based data assurance. Findings The conceptual analysis suggests that Metaverse technologies may create virtual environments capable of replicating physical supply chain dynamics, enabling proactive identification of vulnerabilities and testing of alternative strategies. Digital twins can support predictive stress-testing, AI may enhance forecasting accuracy and AR–VR can strengthen training and preparedness. Blockchain contributes to data security and traceability. Together, these tools can support the adaptability and responsiveness of supply chains. Practical implications The framework provides guidance for firms to evaluate vulnerabilities, simulate disruption scenarios and enhance operational readiness through real-time feedback and virtual training environments. Originality/value The study offers a comprehensive framework illustrating how i

latest.title: The effect of design thinking on knowledge quality: the role of innovation capability and information technology-enabled capability
latest.abstract: Purpose Organizations increasingly depend on creating and using high-quality knowledge resources to sustain innovation and knowledge-informed decision-making. This study aims to examine how design thinking, conceptualized as a knowledge-mobilization practice, is associated with perceived knowledge quality through innovation capability, and whether IT-enabled capability (measured through customer and market analytics) conditions the first stage of this pathway. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees of organizations operating across four sectors: IT/technology, manufacturing, services and education/research. Established measurement scales were adopted or adapted to assess all constructs. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to evaluate the measurement model and to test the hypothesized direct, mediating and moderating relationships. Findings Design thinking was positively associated with both innovation capability and knowledge quality, and innovation capability was positively associated with knowledge quality. The indirect effect through innovation capability was statistically significant but small, a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation in which innovation capability is a meaningful but incremental mechanism. IT-enabled capability positively moderates the association between design thinking and innovation capability, but the index of moderated mediation was not statistically significant, so the moderated mediation hypothesis (H6) was not supported and the full moderated-mediation mechanism is not confirmed. The model explained limited variance, and the cross-sectional, self-reported design does not allow causal conclusions. Originality/value The study reverses the convent

latest.title: Revolutionizing e-retailing: how artificial intelligence shapes consumer purchase intentions?
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) has been revolutionizing consumer behavior in e-retailing. As AI transforms online shopping experiences through personalization, recommendation systems and virtual assistants, understanding how consumers evaluate and engage with these technologies is becoming increasingly important. This study aims to examine the influence of personal activation factors (subjective norms, faith and conscientiousness) on purchase intention in e-retailing, while considering the mediating roles of AI-enabled ease of use and perceived quality of AI services. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 1,438 Portuguese consumers who use AI in their e-retail interactions, this research adopts a quantitative approach using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Findings The findings of this study reveal that all three factors have a positive influence on both AI-enabled ease of use and the perceived quality of AI services, which in turn significantly affect purchase intention. Particularly, conscientiousness has the strongest influence on ease of use, while subjective norms have the most significant impact on perceived service quality. This study also confirms that both mediators, AI-enabled ease of use and quality of AI service, have a positive effect on purchase intention, although the mediating effect slightly weakens the direct relationship between personal factors and purchase decisions. Originality/value These results highlight the importance for e-retailers to design targeted marketing strategies that leverage consumer subjective norms, faith and conscientiousness to effectively translate AI usability and service quality into increased purchase intentions.

latest.title: The challenge of signalling consistency: a comparative case study of hybrid human–AI coaching implementation
latest.abstract: Purpose AI is transforming organisational HRD practices, including workplace coaching. Hybrid human–AI coaching, in which employees are coached by both a human and an AI coach, introduces interpretive ambiguity about the nature of coaching and the roles human and AI agents play. Using the Consolidated Framework of Implementation Research (CFIR) and HR System Strength Theory (HR SST), we explored barriers and facilitators to implementing hybrid human–AI coaching in organisations and how stakeholders make sense of it. Design/methodology/approach Our qualitative comparative case study drew from 17 semi-structured interviews with multiple stakeholders (HR professionals, the AIC provider, human coaches and coachees) from two organisations that implemented hybrid coaching. Hybrid deductive-inductive thematic analysis identified key barriers and facilitators within the CFIR domains, condensed into the three determinants of HR SST. Findings Factors influencing implementation include strategic positioning, human–AI alignment, cultural fit and stakeholder engagement and co-design. Differences in the HR SST determinants distinctiveness (i.e. strategic vs. ad-hoc HRD practice) and stakeholder consensus (e.g. management engagement) shaped diverging implementation trajectories between the two cases. Consistency, especially regarding human–AI coaching alignment, was a critical shared challenge. Originality/value We show that implementing hybrid human–AI coaching involves a complex process of organisational sensemaking that must be managed carefully with the HR SST determinants in mind. Our study extends HR SST by demonstrating that consistency is a challenge not only across HR practices but also within dual-agent HRD practices such as hybrid coaching. It also shows how hybrid human–AI

latest.title: The Multifaceted Nature of Porn as Leisure
latest.venue: International Journal of the Sociology of Leisure
latest.abstract: This study investigated the multifaceted nature of porn use among adults. In-depth interviews were conducted with eleven adults (7 female and 4 male) who have varying sexual orientations, racial backgrounds, and education levels. Using a qualitative approach informed by constructive grounded theory, interview data was analyzed through techniques of initial and focused coding which revealed the experiences of porn use are complex, multi-faceted, and have leisure and non-leisure functions. Participants engaged across various mediums, favoring niche sites and high-quality content. Porn use as leisure was described as enhancing autonomy, intimacy, and communication, contributing to empowerment and quality of life. Yet, participants also shared negative aspects of their porn use, including shame, excessive use, and unrealistic sexual expectations, illustrating porn’s duality as both pleasurable and distressing. Findings suggest that porn use may support mental health when experienced as freely chosen and aligned with personal values, but may contribute to distress, guilt, and shame when perceived as constrained and/or in conflict with social or moral norms, underscoring how well-being is shaped by the experience of leisure.

latest.title: Industrial Information Integration-Selected Patents and Innovations
latest.venue: Journal of Emerging Technologies With Industrial Applications
latest.abstract: Industrial information integration has been mapped repeatedly on its academic side, through a series of literature reviews spanning two decades of research. Its patent record, what firms build, protect, and commercialize, has not been mapped at all. This paper provides the first systematic survey of that record. From the Lens.org database we retrieve 6627 unique patent families that use the phrase “information integration” and were published between January 2006 and July 2026 across the United States, European, German, and Chinese patent offices, screen them to an in-scope pool of 3312 families, and classify the pool along two separately coded dimensions: the integration mechanism, in seven classes (five mapped to layers of IEC 62264 and RAMI 4.0 and two cross-cutting capability classes), and the application domain, in nine classes aligned with the research-category framework of the parent review series. From this pool, 150 families are selected by a composite representativeness score and manually coded under a written codebook, yielding a descriptive corpus of 116 representative patent families that are introduced individually by domain along the industrial value chain. Annual patenting volume grows roughly threefold across the window when families are dated by their first publication, accelerating after 2015. The two dominant patenting systems differ structurally rather than only in volume: in the retrieved corpus, families published through the US office are concentrated among large vendors, with the ten largest applicant groups holding 26.5% of families, while families published through the Chinese office are more fragmented, with the ten largest holding 10.3% and led by a utility rather than a technology vendor. Patenting concentrates in the data and model classes

latest.title: Informal Customer Relationship Management in B2B Healthcare Distribution: Empirical Insights from a Small Medical Consumables Distributor in India
latest.abstract: While there is a lot of academic research on the use of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) in the healthcare sector, this mostly focuses on the use of CRM in large enterprises such as hospitals and pharmaceutical companies. This research aims to provide some insights into how CRM is used in the distribution of medical consumables by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the healthcare sector, in the context of the low level of digitization in B2B transactions in India. The study is based on structured field observations and thematic activity coding of 25 working days (five weeks) in a small medical consumables distributor in Navi Mumbai. Quantitative time-allocation analysis of the various activities of the company’s marketing team showed that, while 32% of their time was spent on manual maintenance of the company’s customer database (in the form of spreadsheets) and on hospital market research, only 12% of their time was spent on follow-up with customers. However, the latter activity was found to be the key driver of the company’s account continuity. Competitor benchmarking of the various products distributed by the company showed that, as the company’s products are identical to those distributed by its competitors, the company can only differentiate itself on the basis of its delivery reliability and the speed with which it can fulfill urgent orders. The study concludes with a zero-cost-to-low-cost phased roadmap for the company to transition from its current reactive spreadsheet-based CRM system to a more structured and formal CRM system.

latest.title: Contracting for Buyer Control of Generative Artificial Intelligence Platforms in Chinese Higher Education
latest.venue: Journal of Organizations Technology and Entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: When a university buys a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform through an integrator, it must decide which tasks its own staff need to perform if the service changes or the contract ends. This study follows that decision from tender specifications into supplier evaluation in Chinese higher education. Of 31 awards examined, 17 concerned application-led purchases. Linked tender and award records were coded for model substitutability, interface interoperability, asset migration and contractual handover. Five application-led lots specified a route to alternative models, two specified external interface rules and three called for reusable asset export or migration. In Fuzhou, two of six qualified suppliers failed technical conformity at the overall demonstration stage. In a mixed software and hardware tender in Zhejiang, the 5.49-point lead exceeded the combined 4.40-point range of four model-access and interface items. With the bidder set and other scores fixed, deleting those items left a minimum lead of 1.09 points. These cases distinguish an eligibility safeguard from a scored preference and show when published records suffice to check whether selected criteria could have affected an award.

latest.title: Algorithmic benevolence or responsibility coercion? How AI-generated content information types shape green purchase intention
latest.abstract: Whether Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) subtly promotes green consumption or triggers consumer resistance remains theoretically underexplored. Drawing on responsibility internalization theory and psychological reactance theory, this study conducted three online studies to examine the mechanisms through which AIGC information types (evidence-oriented vs. value-oriented) influence consumers’ green purchase intention. The results indicate that value-oriented information generates higher green purchase intentions than evidence-oriented information, while simultaneously eliciting stronger responsibility internalization and perceptions of autonomy threat. Further analysis reveals that power distance belief (PDB) plays a significant moderating role in the relationship between information types and two psychological responses. Additionally, perceived consumer effectiveness (PCE) moderates the outcomes of these dual psychological mechanisms; high PCE not only reinforces the positive impact of responsibility internalization on green purchase intentions but also, to some extent, mitigates the resistance effect triggered by autonomy threats. This study reveals the “double-edged sword” effect of generative AI (GAI) in green marketing, offering valuable practical guidance for enterprises to optimize GAI communication strategies and enhance green marketing effectiveness.

latest.title: AI-Powered Business Intelligence and Advanced Decision Analytics for Improving Enterprise Performance and Digital Competitiveness in Saudi Arabia
latest.abstract: Saudi enterprises are spending heavily on dashboards, data platforms and artificial intelligence (AI), yet the link between these investments and measurable performance is often assumed rather than demonstrated. This review asks how AI-powered business intelligence and advanced decision analytics create enterprise value, which conditions govern that value in Saudi organisations, and how managers can steer analytics investment towards digital competitiveness. A systematic integrative review was conducted of 30 peer-reviewed journal studies published between 2020 and 2025. It was anchored by a survey of business analytics experts in Saudi firms that examined innovation capabilities as a mediator, and by a study of AI capability, data-driven culture and firm performance. Eleven of the 30 studies report evidence from the Kingdom. Three findings stand out. First, analytics and AI improve performance mainly through better and faster decisions, organisational learning and innovation, rather than through technology alone, and data-driven culture and employee analytics skills repeatedly act as the transmission belt. Second, Saudi evidence shows that organisational factors, management support, security and human capital matter more for adoption and performance than infrastructure per se, while recent panel studies associate AI and digital transformation with stronger environmental, social and governance results among listed firms. Third, the appropriate division of labour between managers and algorithms depends on how structured and uncertain a decision is. The paper proposes a decision-value framework that links capability resources, decision modes, performance outcomes and competitiveness, together with a matrix for allocating decisions between automation, augmentation and huma

latest.title: Capabilities of Internal Audit to Assess Cost-Effectiveness of Wearable Health Monitoring Systems
latest.venue: International Journal of Online and Biomedical Engineering (iJOE)
latest.abstract: The aim of the current research study is to shed light on the aspects of internal audit, including technical competency, risk-based auditing, compliance and regulatory auditing, valuefor-money (VfM), vendor and contract management that have the ability to assess the cost-effectiveness of wearable health monitoring systems in Jordan. We depended on quantitative methodology to collect primary data through a questionnaire from 388 healthcare system auditors in Jordan. The main objective of the study is to investigate the ability to measure the cost-effectiveness of wearable health monitoring systems in Jordan’s healthcare sector through the use of the internal audit previously mentioned dimensions. It is expected from the study to have theoretical and practical implications. Theoretically, the study contributes to audit theory by adding to the existing internal audit frameworks in digital health technology environments in developing economies. Practically, the results will help Jordanian healthcare institutions enhance the skills of their auditors, optimize investments in the wearable health monitoring systems (WHMS), and establish national standards for audits according to the national agenda for digitalization of the healthcare system.

latest.title: ДОБРОЧЕСНІСТЬ У ЦИФРОВІЙ КОМУНІКАЦІЇ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ ГОТЕЛЬНО-РЕСТОРАННОЇ СФЕРИ
latest.abstract: The article examines digital integrity as a comprehensive characteristic of communication in hospitality enterprises, encompassing information accuracy, transparency of commercial offers, appropriate use of customer reviews, advertising disclosure, personal data protection, and responsible use of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence. The purpose of the study is to identify the main criteria of digital integrity in the HoReCa sector and apply them to the online communication of the ChaCha restaurant in Kropyvnytskyi, Ukraine. The research methodology combines analysis of Ukrainian legal acts, descriptive and comparative analysis of information presented across digital channels, and synthesis of the practices identified. The empirical material includes the restaurant’s official website, the Mister.Am delivery platform, and the TOP20 information and rating platform. The study analyses information on opening hours, address, menu, prices, discounts, delivery, takeaway, and online reviews. The findings demonstrate that digital integrity involves more than the absence of false information. It requires consistency across digital platforms, accessibility of essential purchasing conditions, transparent processing of personal data, authenticity of customer reviews, and appropriate oversight of algorithmically generated content. The study systematizes risks associated with manipulative digital communication, including concealed restrictions on promotions and additional charges, artificial urgency, misleading images, selective presentation of reviews, and automated responses without human supervision. The review of ChaCha’s accessible digital channels revealed no obvious signs of deliberate concealment of offer conditions or artificial pressure on customers to mak

latest.title: Digital Transformation and Cross-Border Supply Chain Coordination: A Review of Research on Mechanisms for Trade Model Innovation
latest.abstract: The current paper synthesizes the pertinent evidence on the topic, combines multidisciplinary concepts, examines the internal transmission channels between the three factors, and develops an analytical framework of how digital transformation leads to innovation in the cross-border trade models. The study critically examines the existing literature and evidence on the topic, synthesizes across disciplines, and develops an analytical model of the internal transmission channels among these three factors, and how the digital transformation facilitates innovation in the cross-border trade patterns. This essay affirms that digital transformation is the key driver of innovation in cross-border trade models. It inspires the transformation of cross-border trade to be more diverse, efficient and of high quality and added value by leveraging supply chain collaboration to transform the trade value chain. This research adds value to the theoretical framework of harmonizing the digital economy with cross-border trade, offering practical advice to the digital transformation of enterprises and the optimization of cross-border supply chains and providing empirical evidence to the development of appropriate policies.

latest.title: Algorithmic Gatekeepers in the Generative AI Era: Platform Asymmetry in AI-Mediated Business Visibility
latest.abstract: The rapid proliferation of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) is fundamentally reshaping digital intermediation.Unlike traditional search engines that rank hyperlinks, generative AI agents synthesize and directly endorse commercial entities, acting as novel algorithmic gatekeepers.However, the structural dynamics of this AI-mediated commercial visibility remain largely unexamined.This study investigates platform asymmetry, industry specialization, and geographical consistency in AI business recommendations.Utilizing the AI Visibility Index, we analyze 79,077 businesslevel observations across 44 industries and 20 countries, auditing the zero-shot recommendation behaviors of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok.Our findings reveal profound structural asymmetry and severe crossplatform fragmentation.Gemini emerges as the dominant intermediary, capturing approximately 50% of the normalized visibility share and leading in 35 of 44 industries, particularly in local and consumer-facing services.Conversely, Claude demonstrates distinct specialization, dominating nine highly regulated, B2B, and financial sectors.Furthermore, we identify severe epistemic fragmentation, with only 261 businesslocation category combinations achieving visibility across all four platforms.These findings challenge foundational marketing paradigms, notably Keller's Customer-Based Brand Equity framework, by demonstrating that brand salience is now strictly contingent upon "algorithmic access."We discuss the imperative for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), the strategic necessity of platform specific visibility management, and the urgent need for regulatory frameworks to address the opaque market shaping power of agentic AI gatekeepers.

latest.title: Parental information, motivation, and self-efficacy in toddler skincare brand preference: an Information–Motivation–Behavioural Skills framework
latest.abstract: Introduction Growing awareness of toddler well-being and the availability of specialized skincare products have increased parental attention to skincare choices. This study examines the relationships of parental knowledge, brand awareness, parental attitude, perceived social norms, and perceived effectiveness with skincare brand preference, while investigating the mediating role of self-efficacy within the Information–Motivation–Behavioural Skills (IMB) framework. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 126 parents recruited through convenience sampling. Data were collected using a structured Google Forms questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model was assessed for reliability and validity, while the structural model was evaluated using path coefficients, bootstrapping, and the coefficient of determination (R 2). Results Parental knowledge, brand awareness, parental attitude, and perceived social norms did not show statistically significant direct relationships with skincare brand preference. Perceived effectiveness demonstrated a significant positive relationship with skincare brand preference (β = 0.576, p = 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed significant indirect through self-efficacy for parental attitude (β = 0.083, p = 0.031) and perceived effectiveness (β = 0.208, p = 0.001). The indirect relationships involving parental knowledge, brand awareness, and perceived social norms were not statistically significant. Discussion The findings highlight the relevance of perceived product effectiveness and self-efficacy in understanding parental skincare brand preferences. The study offers implications for health communication, consumer education, and responsible marketing of

latest.title: Toward Personalized Neurofeedback for Meditation
latest.abstract: Objectives Neurotechnological tools that provide real-time feedback during meditation have generated growing interest as potential aids for accelerating contemplative learning and enhancing mental health outcomes. Currently, the empirical evidence for neurofeedback-assisted meditation is preliminary, and many systems rely on generalized neural targets that may overlook substantial individual variability. Methods This conceptual paper draws on a narrative (non-systematic) synthesis of the literature to propose a testable research agenda, address limitations of neurofeedback, and outline necessary community partnerships. Results Current evidence is limited in demonstrating durable or transferable improvements in meditative skill. In the realm of meditation, individual variability can markedly affect how users respond to protocols and acquire meditative skills. Personalized interventions, tailored to these individual differences, are thus identified as a potential research direction within the field. Conclusions We propose an embrace of individual differences to guide the development of personalized neurotechnological interventions (a “qualia compass” calibrated to each practitioner), on the premise that personalization may increase efficacy and reduce adverse effects. As interest in the cognitive and health benefits of meditation continues to grow, the philosophical and cultural challenges involved in translating these contemplative practices into neurotechnological frameworks also require consideration. Although these complexities emphasize the importance of individualized, multimodal approaches, a personalized approach alone is insufficient to ensure the effective and ethical integration of neurofeedback into the modern mindfulness movement. latest.title: Secondary Appraisal: The Impact of Perceived Control on Challenge and Hindrance Technostress
latest.abstract: The perception of technostress as a challenge or hindrance is shaped by primary and secondary appraisals. However, cognitive appraisal mechanisms remain insufficiently specified because prior research has emphasized primary appraisals, while overlooking secondary appraisals, particularly perceptions of control. The role of control in determining whether information systems (IS) use demands are evaluated as challenges or hindrances is critical, influencing coping strategies and job outcomes. Therefore, this paper theorizes and contextualizes three distinct types of control: ‘control over self’ (e.g., the ability to regulate impulsive behavior), ‘control over work’ (e.g., perceived autonomy), and ‘control over IT’ (e.g., influence over IS functionalities). We investigate how these types of control affect challenge and hindrance appraisals, coping strategies, and subsequent job outcomes. The results demonstrate that these three types of control have various effects and result in coping strategies and job outcomes. The present study makes a significant contribution to the extant literature by highlighting the significance of secondary appraisal, clarifying the differentiated effects of three forms of control, and showing how they influence primary appraisal, coping strategies, and IT-enabled productivity.

latest.title: Pengaruh Personalisasi Rekomendasi Produk Terhadap Perilaku Pembelian Konsumen Dengan Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase Behavior, and the mediating role of Trust among Shopee users based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling, resulting in 111 eligible respondents, comprising 72.07% male and 27.93% female respondents aged 14–69 years. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results indicate that Product Recommendation Personalization has a positive and significant effect on Trust (β = 0.696; p < 0.001). Trust also has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Behavior (β = 0.719; p < 0.001). The indirect effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Purchase Behavior through Trust is also significant (β = 0.501; p < 0.001), confirming the mediating role of Trust. These findings support the S-O-R mechanism and highlight the importance of recommendation relevance and user trust in supporting online purchasing behavior.

latest.title: Determinasi Brand Evangelism Hasil Personalisasi, Influencer–Brand Fit, Dan Perceived Authenticity Melalui Consumer Trust
latest.abstract: The emergence of social media as a marketing tool has transformed consumer behavior toward brands. This study aims to analyze the effects of personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity on brand evangelism, with consumer trust as a mediating variable. This study employs a quantitative approach through a survey of 268 social media users selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the SmartPLS software. The results show that personalization level, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust have a positive effect on brand evangelism. In addition, personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity have a positive effect on consumer trust. However, influencer–brand fit does not have a significant direct effect on brand evangelism. These findings underscore the importance of personalization, authenticity, and consumer trust in driving brand evangelism on social media.

latest.title: Financial Distress in Indonesian Retail Companies: Prediction Model Performance and Financial and Macroeconomic Determinants
latest.abstract: Financial distress poses risks to Indonesian retail companies amid changing sales conditions and financial pressures, making early detection reliable and timely. This study compares the classification performance of the Altman Z-Score, Zmijewski X-Score, and Grover G-Score against a Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) benchmark and examines how fundamental and macroeconomic factors affect distress. A quantitative approach uses secondary quarterly data from 19 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024, yielding 380 observations. Model performance is evaluated using confusion matrices and classification metrics, followed by random-effects panel regressions with robust standard errors using DSCR and the best-performing model’s score as dependent variables. Zmijewski performs best, with 81.3% accuracy, 78.4% balanced accuracy, and a 40.0% false negative rate. DAR is negatively associated with DSCR, while TATO is positively associated with DSCR; ROA is positive at the 10% significance level. Firm size is negatively associated with the Zmijewski score. CR, GDP, and the BI Rate are not significant in the respective models, while inflation is positively associated with DSCR only. The findings support combining model-based screening with financial and macroeconomic monitoring.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kredibilitas Affiliate Marketing dan Kepercayaan Konsumen terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk di TikTok Shop
latest.venue: Best Journal of Administration and Management
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of affiliate marketing credibility and consumer trust on purchase decisions for products on TikTok Shop, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative explanatory design was employed. The population comprised TikTok Shop users who had purchased products through affiliate content, and 350 respondents were selected by purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire with 15 five-point Likert items measuring affiliate marketing credibility (expertise, honesty, communicator attractiveness, information credibility, and consistency), consumer trust (seller integrity, transaction reliability, transaction security, product conformity, and promise fulfilment), and purchase decision (product, brand, seller, timing, and quantity choice). All items were valid (corrected item-total r = 0.604–0.724) and reliable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.836–0.861), and the classical assumptions were met. Multiple linear regression showed that affiliate marketing credibility had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (B = 0.434; t = 9.542; p < 0.001), as did consumer trust (B = 0.273; t = 5.575; p < 0.001). Simultaneously, both variables significantly affected purchase decisions (F = 82.239; p < 0.001) and explained 32.2% of its variance. Affiliate credibility was the dominant predictor (beta = 0.439). Sellers and brands should therefore recruit knowledgeable and honest affiliates while strengthening transaction security and product conformity to convert affiliate exposure into purchases.

latest.title: AI-enabled HR practices and employee-perceived customer experience outcomes in retail services: the mediating role of frontline employee engagement
latest.abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in human resource (HR) functions is transforming how retail service organizations manage frontline employees and deliver customer experiences. Although previous studies have examined AI in HR primarily in terms of efficiency and cost, limited research has explored its association with customer experience-related outcomes through employee processes. This study examines the relationship between AI-enabled HR practices and customer experience outcomes in retail services, focusing on the mediating role of frontline employee engagement. Drawing on social exchange theory, the study proposes that AI-enabled HR practices, including AI-based performance feedback, personalized training, and intelligent workforce scheduling, are associated with stronger frontline employee engagement. The proposed relationships were examined using cross-sectional survey data from 242 frontline retail employees through structural equation modeling. Customer service quality and customer satisfaction were assessed from employees’ perceptions of customer-facing service outcomes rather than direct customer responses. Results indicate positive associations between AI-enabled HR practices and frontline employee engagement, and between engagement and employee-perceived customer service quality and satisfaction. Bootstrapped mediation analysis further indicates significant indirect pathways through frontline employee engagement. The findings extend AI-HRM research into the retail service context and highlight the importance of employee engagement in connecting AI-enabled HR practices with customer-facing service outcomes.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Integrated Optimization of Environmental Impacts and Profit in a Virtual Closed-Loop Supply Chain Based on Blockchain and Wireless Sensor Network
latest.abstract: This article presents a multi-echelon, multi-period, and multi-product model with two objectives: profit maximization and minimization of adverse environmental impacts. The proposed model optimizes a virtual green closed-loop supply chain using wireless sensor network and blockchain technologies for real-time data collection and enhanced transparency, respectively. A mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated, encompassing forward flows across four echelons and reverse flows across three echelons. Moreover, a fuzzy number approach addresses demand uncertainty. Small- and medium- scale problems are solved with GAMS, whereas large-scale problems are addressed using the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer due to their NP-hard nature. Two comparative studies evaluate digital technologies: the first examines concurrent deployment of wireless sensor network and blockchain, while the second highlights blockchain's role. Compared with the model without these technologies, the integrated deployment of wireless sensor networks and blockchain increases supply chain profit by 37.25%, improves demand fulfillment rate by 3.82%, and reduces total adverse environmental impacts by 7.69%. Moreover, compared with the model equipped solely with a wireless sensor network, the integrated deployment of the technologies increases profit by 10.66%, improves the demand fulfillment by 2.33%, and reduces total adverse environmental impacts by 4.29%. These findings indicate that joint deployment enhances supply chain performance through improved coordination, returned-product identification, recovery efficiency, and demand fulfillment, particularly under high forward and reverse flow intensity. Accordingly, managers can evaluate digital investments at the supply chain level and prioritize

latest.title: Social Influence in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Preference for Humans Does Not Deter Artificial Intelligence Influence
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a source of social influence. But people often prefer human over AI sources (algorithm aversion/preference for humans), which might prevent AI from influencing humans. However, we outline a theoretical framework that suggests that preferences do not play a causal role in influence. To test this framework, we investigated under which conditions preferences predict AI influence. Participants (N = 1,254) indicated their adviser preference and then made incentivised decisions while receiving advice from AI or human advisers. Participants preferred human over AI advisers but were influenced by AI and humans similarly. A strong aversion to AI advisers had no (Study 1) or a trivial relation (Study 2 and 3) with AI influence, which was explained by confounding variables. When manipulated, preferences did not predict advice-taking, but adviser trustworthiness and competence did (Study 3). Our results suggest that for predicting AI influence, understanding domain-specific social cognitions, not preferences, is critical.

latest.title: Designing competitive generative AI services: Consumer preferences and pricing implications for SMEs and venture companies
latest.abstract: This study examines consumer preferences for generative AI (GenAI) services and explores how these preferences influence willingness to pay (WTP) and market competitiveness, with a particular focus on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and venture companies. As GenAI technologies rapidly evolve and the application service market expands, understanding how consumers evaluate different service attributes becomes critical for designing competitive and sustainable business models. This study employs a conjoint analysis combined with a mixed logit model to capture consumer heterogeneity and analyze trade-offs among key service attributes. Six attributes are considered: purpose of use, data accuracy and timeliness, disclosure of data sources, data bias and personal information verification, type of service provider, and service fees. The results indicate that consumers place the greatest importance on service fees, followed by trust-related attributes such as data accuracy, verification, and transparency. In addition, the findings reveal no statistically significant preference for large global or domestic firms, while SMEs and venture companies are positively and significantly preferred, suggesting that competitive advantage in the GenAI application market may depend more on service design than on firm size. These findings contribute to the literature by providing an integrated analysis of consumer preference structures and pricing in the GenAI service market. From a practical perspective, the study offers strategic insights for SMEs and venture companies, emphasizing the importance of trust-enhancing features and value-based pricing strategies in achieving sustainable competitiveness.

latest.title: Factors Influencing Foreign Portfolio Investment in South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) Countries
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Research and Economics
latest.abstract: This study examines the determinants of FPI in the SAARC countries over the period 2010-2024. Using panel data regression with a Random Effects Model (REM), the study analyzes the influence of Exchange Rate, Market Size, and Digital Infrastructure, as represented by Internet Users (% of Population), on FPI. The results show that “Exchange Rate has a positive and significant effect on FPI, while Market Size has a negative and significant effect. Meanwhile, Digital Infrastructure shows an insignificant negative effect on FPI.” These findings suggest that foreign portfolio investors place more emphasis on macroeconomic fundamentals than digital developments when making investment decisions. The novelty of this study lies in its examination of digital infrastructure through Internet Users as a proxy for information absorption capacity based on the Information Cost Theory. The results of this study contrast with the view that digitalization automatically increases international capital inflows, highlighting that economic, fundamentals remain the primary driver of FPI in SAARC countries.

latest.title: Driving Private University Choice: A Combined PLS-SEM, IPMA, and NCA Analysis of Brand Image and Trust
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Brand Image and Trust drive prospective students’ private university choices in Bandung. We examine both direct structural relationships and the necessary prerequisite conditions required to optimize institutional enrollment. To conduct this investigation, the authors surveyed 100 university students using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. This study subsequently analyzed the quantitative data utilizing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS to assess path relationships and predictive power. Finally, the analytical framework integrated Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) to identify operational priorities and critical bottleneck thresholds. The PLS-SEM path analysis confirms that Brand Image directly drives Student Choice (β = 0.411) and significantly mediates the impact of Trust (β = 0.325), while Trust serves as the primary predictor of Brand Image (β = 0.790, R2 = 0.572). IPMA identifies Trust—specifically Benevolence and Integrity—as the highest-leverage area for institutional improvement due to its high overall importance (0.713) but lower current performance (50.500). Furthermore, NCA reveals that Brand Benefits (d = 0.526) and Benevolence (d = 0.428) act as indispensable necessary conditions, establishing that achieving top-tier enrollment outcomes (90%–100%) requires high minimum bottleneck capacities in Brand (68%) and Trust (73%). Implications for institutional management, must allocate resources strategically by first satisfying essential bottleneck conditions. Institutions should guarantee clear Brand Benefits and show institutional Benevolence to avoid enrollment barriers, while enhancing Integrity to build long-term brand equity and secure stu

latest.title: Earnings Management of Oil & Gas Firms After the Russian Invasion of Ukraine
latest.abstract: Political crises often lead to sharp increases in energy prices and, consequently, in the profits of oil and gas companies. However, exceptionally high profits may be perceived as unethical, creating reputational and legitimacy concerns that can influence firms’ financial reporting behavior. Yet, there is no evidence whether European oil & gas firms manage earnings after sudden political crises, and whether their responses differ across countries. Using a difference-in-differences design, this study documents that European oil & gas firms engaged in significant income-decreasing earnings management—through both accrual-based and real activities—following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. This effect is particularly pronounced in the third quarter of 2022 and the first quarter of 2023. We further find that (real) earnings management by oil & gas firms is more pronounced in countries that implemented windfall profit taxes and in institutional environments characterized by stronger democratic governance. At the firm level, the effect is concentrated among oil & gas firms with relatively low sustainability scores, which exhibit significantly greater income-decreasing earnings management than control firms. These findings suggest that earnings management decisions were driven not only by tax considerations but also by legitimacy and reputational concerns. This study contributes to the literature by providing cross-country evidence that exploits variation in taxation regimes and institutional settings, and by explicitly examining the role of legitimacy and reputational concerns in shaping corporate reporting behavior.

latest.title: Consumer response to a multi-channel promotional campaign for local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq: a mixed-methods evaluation
latest.abstract: Introduction This study looked at how a multi-channel promotional campaign, affected what people know, how they feel, and whether they actually bought local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methods A single cohort of 400 consumers was surveyed before the campaign (September–October 2025) and re-contacted after campaign implementation (July–August 2026). After matching respondents, we were able to compare 165 individuals with confidence. Our questionnaire covered knowledge, attitudes, buying habits, campaign exposure and recognition (distinguishing visibility, engagement, and message recall), message quality, barriers to purchase, and willingness to pay. We used a mix of statistical tools, from simple comparisons to more advanced techniques like regression analysis and clustering. Results Knowledge increased significantly from pre-campaign (2.621 ± 0.904) to post-campaign (2.903 ± 0.992; Δ = +0.282, p = 0.003, Cohen’s dz. = 0.236). No statistically significant overall changes were detected in attitudes (Δ = +0.074, p = 0.328) or purchasing behavior (Δ = −0.012, p = 0.872). Overall campaign exposure was moderate (2.653/5), with social media exposure higher than traditional media. Barriers to purchasing included insufficient label information (3.313), difficulty finding the product (3.275), and weak packaging/branding (3.258). PCA identified eight underlying dimensions explaining 63.3% of variance, and K-means clustering produced five exploratory consumer profiles: “Informed but barrier-constrained engaged consumers” (21.0%); “Low-engagement/low-response consumers” (17.0%); “Committed local-olive-oil advocates” (29.5%); “Under-reached but potentially receptive consumers” (8.2%); and “Positive but underinformed consumers” (24.2%). Discussion The big takeaway is th

latest.title: The Influence of Risk Management on Business Sustainability Mediated by Environmental Performance
latest.abstract: Businesses face increasing environmental pressures, regulatory requirements, and operational uncertainties that threaten their long-term viability. Risk management is widely recognized as a strategic approach to anticipating and mitigating these challenges; however, its contribution to business sustainability remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationship between risk management and business sustainability, with environmental performance serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative research approach was employed, and primary data were collected from 100 respondents using an online questionnaire administered through Google Forms. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling with partial least squares (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS software, encompassing measurement model assessment, structural model evaluation, and mediation analysis. The findings revealed that risk management did not have a statistically significant direct effect on business sustainability but had a significant positive effect on environmental performance. Furthermore, environmental performance significantly influenced business sustainability and mediated the relationship between risk management and business sustainability. These findings suggest that effective risk management contributes to business sustainability primarily through improvements in environmental performance rather than through a direct relationship. Environmental performance therefore serves as a key mediating mechanism through which risk management practices contribute to long-term business sustainability. The study highlights the importance of integrating risk management strategies with measurable environmental performance improvements to strengthen organizational resilience and support sus

latest.title: Digitalization, Green Innovation, and SME Performance in Emerging Economies: The Mediating Role of Cultural Capability and the Reinforcing Role of HRM Practices
latest.abstract: This study examines how digitalization and green innovation influence perceived firm performance by investigating the mediating role of cultural capability and the moderating role of human resource management (HRM) practices. Drawing on the resource‐based view and absorptive capacity theory, data were collected from 399 SMEs in Ghana using a two‐wave survey design and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that digitalization is positively associated with perceived firm performance, whereas green innovation exhibits no significant direct relationship. Both digitalization and green innovation are positively associated with cultural capability; however, cultural capability is negatively associated with perceived firm performance, resulting in significant negative indirect effects that are contrary to the hypothesized positive mediation. HRM practices positively moderate the relationship between cultural capability and perceived firm performance, indicating that stronger HRM practices make this relationship more favorable. These findings reveal a more complex capability–performance relationship than anticipated, suggesting that organizational capability development and deployment do not necessarily correspond with immediate performance gains and that their performance implications may depend on complementary organizational conditions.

latest.title: Architecting AI-Ready Data Ecosystems: A Governed, Scalable and Real-Time Framework for Enterprise Intelligence
latest.venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
latest.abstract: The fragmented, poorly-governed and temporally inconsistent data environment is often the reason why AI initiatives don't go beyond prototypes to enterprise services that can be relied upon. This conceptual review brings together existing literature on data warehouses, data lakes, lakehouses, data mesh, streaming systems, machine-learning operations and retrieval-augmented generation to identify the features of an AI-ready data ecosystem. AI readiness is understood to be the ability to deliver discoverable, semantically consistent, quality-controlled, traceable and timely data for analytical and operational purposes. A five layer reference architecture is suggested, which includes source ingestion, unified storage, processing and quality, semantic and AI enablement, and intelligence consumption. Governance and observability are considered as cross-cutting control planes and feedback from deployed models and applications is fed back to upper layers. The framework connects architectural decisions with quantifiable metrics like ownership coverage, contract adherence, freshness, lineage completeness, quality test pass rate and training-serving consistency. The study shows that lakehouse mechanisms can be used to reliably share a substrate while data-mesh principles can enhance domain accountability with adequate platform automation and interoperability standards. Business latency budgets, not technology labels, should be used to indicate real-time capability. The suggested framework provides a succinct starting point for organisations looking to modernise their data platforms without fragmenting their data scalability, governance and AI operations into distinct programmes.

latest.title: Improving Digital Literacy and Financial Transaction Efficiency Among Msmes in Kampung Parit, Melaka, Malaysia
latest.abstract: This community service activity aims to improve digital literacy and financial transaction efficiency among MSMEs in Kampung Parit, Melaka, Malaysia, through the implementation of an e-wallet-based payment system. Implementation methods include outreach, training on how to use the e-wallet application, and direct assistance in implementing the system in daily buying and selling activities. The results of the activity showed that the majority of MSMEs were able to operate e-wallets independently, making transactions faster, more secure, and digitally recorded, increasing consumer trust. Furthermore, business owners began to experience efficiencies in financial management and sales recording. In conclusion, implementing an e-wallet payment system can be an effective strategy to support the digitalization of MSMEs, increase the competitiveness of small businesses, and expand market access through practical and modern cashless transactions.

latest.title: ESG Ratings as Predictors of Financial Distress: Implications for Sustainable Development, Investment Risk Assessment, and Corporate Resilience
latest.abstract: ESG ratings are increasingly important in sustainable investment screening, although their value for predicting emerging corporate financial distress remains uncertain. This study examines whether aggregate and pillar‐level environmental, social, and governance performance improves the 1‐year‐ahead prediction of entry into an Altman‐based distress zone. The sample comprises 55,557 firm‐year observations from 7698 firms across 37 countries during 2016–2024. Using logistic regression, the ESG Combined Score and individual pillars are compared with a financial baseline containing the five Altman components and firm characteristics. Predictive performance is assessed using model fit, information criteria, discrimination, probability accuracy, and temporal validation. The results show statistically significant associations of ESG but only small predictive enhancements. The ESG Combined Score, environmental performance, and governance performance are negatively associated with the onset of financial distress in the original models, whereas social performance is insignificant when considered separately but positive in the joint model. The joint‐pillar model achieves the best in‐sample fit, while governance performance achieves the highest AUC in the original temporal holdout, although it is not statistically significant. Additional temporal validation suggests that predictive gains vary across periods. Country fixed effects confirm the negative environmental association but reveal sensitivity in aggregate ESG and governance estimates. An alternative Altman distress classification also finds mixed results, while the alternative overall ESG score is insignificant. ESG ratings can complement conventional financial distress screening but contribute differentially to predictive acc

latest.title: Analisis Faktor-Faktor Yang Memengaruhi Innovative Work Behavior Tutor biMBA AIUEO
latest.abstract: The expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI) requires tutors in nonformal educational institutions to continuously renew how they guide learners. This study examines the contributions of AI readiness, digital literacy, and organizational support to the innovative work behavior (IWB) of biMBA AIUEO tutors, with creative self-efficacy (CSE) as a mediating variable. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 44 tutors and analyzed using descriptive statistics, two regression equations within a path analysis framework, and bootstrapping mediation testing via PROCESS Macro Model 4. In the simultaneous model, organizational support had a positive and significant effect on CSE, whereas AI readiness and digital literacy showed no significant effect. In the IWB model, CSE was the only significant direct predictor, while AI readiness, digital literacy, and organizational support had no significant direct effects on IWB. However, bootstrapping with a 95% confidence interval revealed that CSE significantly mediates the relationships between AI readiness, digital literacy, and organizational support and IWB, showing an indirect-only mediation pattern. Because the study involved 44 tutors from a single institutional network, its findings should be generalized with caution
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Sustainability under scrutiny: From corporate greenwashing to environmental verifiability
latest.abstract: The growing importance of sustainability in corporate strategy has placed companies’ environmental statements under a new legal paradigm: it is no longer sufficient to communicate green commitments; they must be proved in a clear, objective, verifiable and legally defensible manner. This article analyses the development of greenwashing from a practice mainly associated with misleading advertising into a structural problem of transparency, regulatory compliance and environmental evidence. To that end, it examines, first, the European and Spanish regulatory framework applicable to environmental claims, with particular regard to the prohibition of generic, vague or unsubstantiated statements, as well as the new requirements for reliable information on corporate sustainability. Secondly, it studies the internal implications for companies, which will have to strengthen their governance systems, coordinate their legal, marketing and sustainability areas, build robust evidential files and anticipate potential litigation or sanctioning proceedings for misleading environmental advertising. Finally, the article addresses the role of verification technologies — satellite observation, artificial intelligence, blockchain, natural language processing and digital auditing — as tools capable of preventing, detecting and evidencing greenwashing practices. The central thesis is that corporate sustainability is entering a phase of reinforced verifiability, in which environmental credibility will depend on organisations’ ability to transform their commitments into traceable data, documented evidence and legally robust controls.

latest.title: Sustainable Investment Initiatives and Corporate Efficiency in Multinational Semiconductor Firms: The Moderating Roles of Business Strategy and Uncertainty Avoidance
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: This study examines how environmental initiatives affect the eco‐efficiency and commercial efficiency of multinational semiconductor firms. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and institutional theory, business strategy is conceptualized as a first‐order moderator and uncertainty avoidance as a second‐order moderator of this relationship. Using a sample of 39 firms across Asia, Europe, and North America over 2018–2022, the analysis integrates a shared‐flow two‐stage data envelopment analysis (DEA) model with hierarchical moderated‐moderation regression, which allows both efficiency dimensions and their contingent determinants to be evaluated within a single framework. The results indicate that a stronger prospector orientation is associated with a more favorable relationship between environmental innovation and commercial efficiency in countries with low uncertainty avoidance, and that this moderating effect weakens as uncertainty avoidance increases. These findings pertain to large, listed semiconductor firms in the sampled countries. They inform policymakers seeking to promote environmental initiatives and offer practical guidance to managers seeking to align environmental objectives with business performance.

latest.title: Job skill demand and thriving at work: mediating roles of AI perceptions and moderating effect of approach motivation
latest.abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of widespread artificial intelligence (AI) integration in organizational settings, this study draws on the Job Demands-Resources model and categorization theory to examine the association between job skill demand and employee thriving at work and its underlying psychological mechanisms, with a focus on the dual mediating roles of AI opportunity perception and AI threat perception, and the moderating effect of approach motivation. Methods A progressive two-study design was adopted with two independent two-wave time-lagged samples of Chinese employees (Study 1: N = 298; Study 2: N = 301). Study 1 preliminarily tested the core main effects, and study 2 replicated the findings and further verified the mediating and moderating mechanisms using hierarchical regression and the PROCESS macro. Results Job skill demand positively predicts AI opportunity perception and negatively predicts AI threat perception. Both opportunity and threat perceptions significantly mediate the relationship between job skill demand and thriving at work. Furthermore, approach motivation significantly moderates the first-stage relationships: it strengthens the positive association between job skill demand and AI opportunity perception and amplifies the negative association between job skill demand and AI threat perception. However, the overall moderated mediation effect does not reach conventional statistical significance. Discussion These findings extend the application of the JD-R model in AI-enabled work contexts and provide practical insights for organizational AI transformation and employee work well-being promotion.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Halal furniture product ınnovation using the quality function deployment (QFD) approach
latest.venue: Mobilya ve Ahşap Malzeme Araştırmaları Dergisi
latest.abstract: The furniture industry in Jepara Regency faces significant challenges in expanding its market share to the global Muslim market, particularly the Middle East, which demands strict halal compliance standards. This study aims to integrate halal values into the technical attributes of furniture design through a Phase 1 Quality Function Deployment (QFD) approach using the House of Quality (HoQ) framework. The research method employed a descriptive quantitative approach using purposive sampling, involving 18 key informants comprising 15 export-oriented furniture industry practitioners and 3 halal auditors. Data collection was conducted through in-depth interviews, a literature review, and structured questionnaires. The results indicate that “Halal Product Assurance” and “Uniqueness of Halal Products” are the primary attributes desired by consumers in the Planning Matrix. In the HoQ matrix, it was found that Modular and Minimalist Design emerged as the top-priority technical responses with a relative weight of 35.45%, followed by the use of Water-Based Finishing Systems at 29.59%. These findings indicate that halal furniture design intrinsically supports the concept of sustainable design (eco-design) by reducing hazardous chemicals and improving product maintainability (thaharah). This study provides a strategic contribution to the furniture manufacturing industry into competitive technical specifications for the international market.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation , each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms.
