latest.title: ANALISIS DESKRIPTIF ORIENTASI PASAR, LOYALITAS PELANGGAN, KEPEMIMPINAN WIRAUSAHAAN, KEPUASAN PELANGGAN, DAN KEBERLANJUTAN UMKM DI KOTA DEPOK
latest.abstract: This study aims to describe market orientation, customer loyalty, entrepreneurial leadership, customer satisfaction, and business sustainability among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Depok City, Indonesia. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed using a survey method. Data were collected through questionnaires using a five-point Likert scale. The study involved 150 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics to identify response patterns across research indicators. The findings indicate that market orientation was rated highly, particularly in meeting customer needs. Entrepreneurial leadership also received high ratings, especially in encouraging innovation and creative problem-solving. Customer satisfaction showed positive results, particularly regarding customer interactions and transaction experiences. Customer loyalty was rated highly, reflected in customers’ willingness to recommend and repurchase products or services. Business sustainability also demonstrated favorable results, particularly in establishing networks and relationships that support business continuity. Overall, MSMEs in Depok City demonstrated relatively favorable conditions across all five variables. These findings provide insights into MSME conditions and may serve as a reference for developing strategies to strengthen business performance and sustainability.Keywords : MSMEs, market orientation, customer loyalty, entrepreneurial leadership, customer satisfaction, business sustainability.

latest.title: Pengaruh Sales Promotion Skincare Facetology di Tiktok terhadap Repurchase Intention: Survei Kepada Followers Akun Tiktok @Facetologyofficial
latest.abstract: The rapid development of social media, particularly TikTok, has prompted skincare companies to optimize their digital marketing to retain consumers. One widely utilizerd digital marketing is sales promotion, which is deemed effective in influencing consumer repurchase intention behavior. This study aims to determine the influence of Facetology skincare’s sales promotion on the repurchase intention of @facetologyoffcial TikTok account followers. This research employs a quantitative approach using a survey method. The population in this study consists of @facetologyofficial TikTok followers, with a sample size of 91 respondents determined using the Slovin formula. Data were collected through the distribution of questionnaires, while data analysis was performed using simple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS version 31 software. The results indicate that sales promotion has a positive and significant effect on repurchase intention. This is evidenced by the t-test results showing a significance value of <0,05 and the ANOVA test confirming the regression model’s feasibility for use. Furthermore, the coefficient of determination (R Square) of 0,758 suggests that sales promotion accounts for 75,8% of the variation in repurchase intention, while the remaining 24,2% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study. latest.title: The mediating role of social identity in the purchase intention for local agri-food products
latest.abstract: Introduction Promoting the consumption of local agri-food products in Baja California, Mexico, is key to strengthening territorial resilience and community sustainability; however, the direct role of subjective norms in the purchase intention for these products remains inconsistent, requiring an investigation of identity-based mechanisms. Accordingly, this research analyzed the mediating role of social identity between the predictors of the theory of planned behavior (attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control) and purchase intention for local agri-food products. Methods An explanatory, quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted. A structured questionnaire was administered online between September and December 2023 to a non-probability purposive sample of 550 adult consumers in Baja California. Data analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the direct and indirect effects within the proposed model. Results The model explained 52.6% of the variance in purchase intention and 46.3% of the variance in social identity. Attitude (β = 0.375, p < 0.001) and perceived behavioral control (β = 0.388, p < 0.001) were the strongest direct predictor of purchase intention. The strongest effect in the model was that of subjective norms on social identity (β = 0.651, p < 0.001). Furthermore, only subjective norms exerted an indirect effect on purchase intention (β = 0.104, p = 0.015) through the full mediation of social identity, as their direct effect remained non-significant (β = -0.609, p = 0.166). Discussion: These findings suggest that social expectations influence the intention to purchase local agri-food products when consumers internalize them as part of their identity, rather than through direct social press

latest.title: Pengaruh Digital Marketing terhadap Peningkatan Dana Pihak Ketiga (DPK) di Bank Syariah Indonesia KCP Pinrang
latest.abstract: Digital transformation in the Islamic banking industry requires sub-branch offices to optimize digital marketing channels in attracting public savings, yet the empirical effectiveness of each digital marketing dimension on increasing Third Party Funds (DPK) at Bank Syariah Indonesia KCP Pinrang remains unclear. This study aims to analyze the partial, simultaneous, and dominant effects of content marketing, social media marketing, digital communication marketing, and digital promotion and mobile marketing on the increase in Third Party Funds (DPK) at BSI KCP Pinrang. This associative quantitative study involved 50 savings customers selected through purposive sampling, sized using Roscoe's guideline. Data were collected through Likert-scale questionnaires, observation, and literature documentation, and analyzed using classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, the t-test, and the F-test via SPSS. Digital communication marketing (B = 0.619; t = 5.037; p < 0.001) had a positive and significant partial effect on increasing DPK, whereas content marketing (B = 0.155; t = 1.313; p = 0.196), social media marketing (B = 0.137; t = 1.361; p = 0.180), and digital promotion and mobile marketing (B = 0.103; t = 0.742; p = 0.462) showed no significant partial effect. Simultaneously, the four dimensions had a significant effect on DPK growth (F = 37.786; p < 0.001), with an Adjusted R Square value of 0.750, indicating that the four dimensions explained 75% of the variance in DPK growth, while the remaining 25% was explained by factors outside the research model. Digital communication marketing (β = 0.562) emerged as the most dominant dimension.

latest.title: The structural alignment of virtual influencers and deepfake endorsers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to understand the effectiveness of virtual influencers versus deepfake endorsers in marketing. It investigates the cognitive processes shaping consumer responses to these digital endorsers. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the structural alignment theory, and across four studies using eye-tracking and experiments, the authors tested various factors, including eeriness, customer engagement, place identity and product manifestations. Findings Deepfake endorsers generally outperform virtual influencers in generating customer engagement and word-of-mouth. Virtual influencers are perceived as more eerie than deepfakes. Deepfakes are more effective in place-based contexts, but virtual influencers are more effective when endorsing NFTs compared to physical products. Research limitations/implications The paper contributes to the structural alignment theory to indicate that customers undergo a cognitive restructuring during the structural alignment process upon perceiving a digital endorser. Practical implications The findings help marketing managers guide the strategic selection of digital endorsers. Developing an endorser portfolio including both deepfake and virtual influencer endorsers is suggested. Matching specific endorsers with campaign target audiences, objectives and product types is recommended. Using different types of digital endorsers at various points in the customer journey can maximize engagement. Originality/value This study is among the first to compare different types of digital endorsers. It contributes to understanding digital endorser effectiveness by highlighting cognitive processes and boundary conditions shaping consumer responses and preferences.

latest.title: Reconfiguring the Marketing Mix: The Effects of Core Marketing Mix, Customer Interface, and Service Experience on Purchase Decisions through Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: RISK Jurnal Riset Bisnis dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Changes in customer behavior require motorcycle repair shops to manage their marketing strategies and customer experiences more strategically. This study examines the effects of Core Marketing Mix, Customer Interface, and Service Experience on Customer Satisfaction and Purchase Decision, as well as the mediating role of Customer Satisfaction. A quantitative approach was applied to data from 200 motorcycle repair shop customers in Malang Regency and Malang Municipality, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that Core Marketing Mix (β = 0.294, p = 0.002) and Customer Interface (β = 0.288, p = 0.025) positively affect Customer Satisfaction, whereas Service Experience has no significant effect (β = −0.006, p = 0.956). All three constructs positively affect Purchase Decision, with Core Marketing Mix showing the strongest effect (β = 0.386, p < 0.001). Customer Satisfaction also positively affects Purchase Decision (β = 0.320, p < 0.001) and mediates the effects of Core Marketing Mix and Customer Interface, but not Service Experience. This study contributes by grouping the 7P marketing elements into three analytical constructs and demonstrating that Customer Satisfaction acts as a selective rather than universal mediator. The findings suggest that motorcycle repair shop managers should prioritize product and price value, customer interactions, and service processes according to their respective effects on purchase decisions

latest.title: Branding Strategies of Home-Based Tempeh Businesses and Consumer Trust amid Changes in the Social Environment
latest.venue: Journal of Business Social and Technology
latest.abstract: Background: Home-based tempeh businesses rely on local reputation and product consistency to maintain consumer trust. Changing consumer preferences and the growing use of digital channels are reshaping how these businesses communicate their identity. Objective: This study examined how home-based tempeh businesses adapted their branding to changes in the social environment and how participants related these practices to consumer trust. Methods: A qualitative multiple-case study examined 12 purposively selected home-based tempeh businesses in Badung, Bali, from September 2024 to January 2025. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with business operators, 24 consumers, and six key informants, supplemented by observations and document analysis. Thematic analysis identified recurring patterns and differences across cases. Results: Businesses communicated family heritage and local identity, engaged customers through community networks and digital channels, maintained product quality, and adapted to changing preferences. Participant accounts linked consumer trust to consistent quality, honest communication, and responsiveness. These findings informed the proposed AKSI framework, comprising Authenticity, Komunitas (community), System, and Innovation. Conclusion: The AKSI framework explains how the branding practices identified in these cases may support consumer trust. Its applicability in other settings and the relative effectiveness of its dimensions require further evaluation.

latest.title: Exploring digital brand personality through logo design: Insights for Thai and Burmese
latest.venue: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences Studies
latest.abstract: When a logo is created with brand personality, this mere visual symbol becomes alive. It enhances the effectiveness of numerous branding strategies and the competitive advantage of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the digital markets. However, existing studies focusing on logo development and brand personality using the three elements—color, shape, and typeface are limited. This study conducted a quantitative online survey with 122 participants (62 Thais and 60 Burmese) aged 18 to 44 years. It aims to 1) study brand personality perceptions towards digital logos designed with color, shape, and typeface and 2) conduct a comparative study of logo design preferences between Thai and Burmese consumers. The findings revealed that 1) some logos conveyed several brand personality dimensions rather than one expected dimension and 2) both Thai and Burmese consumers preferred logo designs similarly. The logo designs that included light colors—green, pink, and white—together with organic shapes and display typefaces were associated with all brand personality dimensions and were also strongly preferred by the participants. This study extends brand personality literature through novel cross-cultural insights from Thailand and Myanmar while providing guidelines to practitioners on how to design logos with suitable brand personality in these emerging markets.

latest.title: Social Customer Relationship Management and Relationship Quality: Evidence from Star-Rated Hotels in Nairobi, Kenya
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
latest.abstract: The main purpose of the study was to establish the effect of Social CRM dimension perceptions on relationship quality in selected hotels in Nairobi, Kenya. The study was anchored in the Malthouse Social CRM House Model and Relationship Marketing Theory. A sequential explanatory research design was adopted, targeting an average of 16,464 customers per month obtained from online hotel bookings, as well as 29 Guest Relations Managers from three purposively selected five-star hotels in Nairobi. A sample of 400 customers was selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected from customers using a structured questionnaire. Quantitative data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings indicated that the data and information dimension and process dimension had a positive and statistically significant effect on relationship quality in hotels. However, the Social CRM strategies dimension had an insignificant effect on relationship quality. Based on these findings, the study recommends that hotels should place greater emphasis on data and information, as well as process-related dimensions, as these significantly influence relationship quality. Although Social CRM strategies were found to have no significant effect, aligning these strategies beyond sales and marketing functions to integrate with organizational processes and data systems could enhance relationship quality. Further, the study recommends that hotel management should invest in training employees on social media use and organizational processes, while continuously monitoring and responding to issues raised on social networks to strengthen customer relationships. The study also contributes to the refinement of the Malthouse Social CRM House Model by improving the process dimension throug

latest.title: Packaging and Product Presentation as Strategic Assets in Marketing and Business: Consumer Evidence, Market Data and Disclosures of NSE-Listed Packaging Companies
latest.abstract: Purpose. To synthesise evidence on how packaging and product presentation work as marketing and business assets, and to examine what the public disclosures of Indian listed packaging companies show about the commercial side of the industry. Design/methodology/approach. A secondary-data study in three parts. First, a synthesis of peer-reviewed research on package design, perception and purchase. Second, a compilation of global and Indian market estimates from industry research firms. Third, a comparison of FY2026 results of five packaging companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), taken from company investor presentations, earnings-call transcripts and results coverage. Every figure was traced to a source and cross-checked against a second source where one existed (Appendix A). Findings. The reviewed studies show that package graphics, shape and technology affect attention, brand impressions, perceived quantity and purchase likelihood, and that convenience-related features carried the most weight in one conjoint study of packaged foods. A US poll for a paper-packaging body found that 72% of respondents agreed packaging design influences their purchases. The global packaging market was about USD 1.2 trillion in 2025 and is forecast to reach USD 1.52 trillion by 2030, while Indian packaging volumes are forecast to grow 5.3% a year to 2030. Among five NSE-listed companies, EBITDA margins ranged from 9.5% to 20.4%, and the two companies with the highest margins, EPL and Mold-Tek Packaging, also grew revenue by about 13%. Research limitations. Secondary data only; a five-company sample chosen for coverage, not at random; correlational comparisons; and a consumer poll funded by an industry body. The propositions are assessed, not tested. Practical implicat

latest.title: Beyond Bricks and Mortar: A Consumer-Centric Approach to Real Estate Marketing in India
latest.abstract: The Indian real estate sector has undergone significant transformation due to technological advancements, increasing market competition and changing consumer expectations. These developments have influenced the ways in which consumers search for, evaluate and purchase properties, making consumer-oriented marketing practices increasingly important. The present study examines the significance of a consumer-centric approach to real estate marketing in India, with particular emphasis on consumer behaviour, trust, transparency, digital marketing and customer experience. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design based entirely on secondary data obtained from academic journals, industry reports, published surveys and other relevant sources. It analyses changing consumer preferences and the role of customer-oriented marketing strategies in influencing property purchase decisions. The study aims to identify marketing practices that can strengthen consumer confidence, enhance customer engagement and support long-term relationships between real estate developers and prospective buyers.

latest.title: The value of thrills: Hedonic pricing in amusement parks
The Role of Digital Marketing in Enhancing Brand Visibility
latest.abstract: Digital tools have changed how companies introduce themselves to the public and stay relevant in everyday consumer life. Instead of relying on one-way print or broadcast campaigns, organizations now build recognition across search engines, social feeds, video platforms, and direct messaging channels. This paper looks at how core digital practices—search engine optimization (SEO), search engine marketing (SEM), social media outreach, content creation, email campaigns, influencer partnerships, and data analytics—help businesses become easier to find and remember. Drawing on twenty studies published between 2021 and 2026, the review shows that getting seen online is only half the battle. High impression counts do not automatically turn into sales. Real commercial growth happens when visibility is backed by consistent brand messaging, useful content, and genuine consumer trust. The paper also points out where current research still falls short—particularly around how multiple channels work together, why audiences grow tired of repetitive ads, and what holds smaller businesses back—before offering practical takeaways for marketers and researchers.

latest.title: Analysis of Determinants of Tourist Revisit Intention: Integration of Destination Quality, Pricing Strategy, and Promotion Effectiveness through Tourist Satisfaction
latest.venue: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing, promotions, brand image and repeat orders on airline consumer loyalty. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by integrating findings from 50 reputable scientific articles sourced from international journals indexed by Scopus, Web of Science, Elsevier, Sage, Emerald, and national journals indexed by SINTA. Literature selection was carried out using strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, with data analysis through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing strengthened by source triangulation. The results of the study indicate that: 1) Destination Quality Integration affects Tourist Satisfaction; 2) Pricing Strategy affects Tourist Satisfaction; 3) Promotion Effectiveness affects Tourist Satisfaction; 4) Destination Quality Integration affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 5) Pricing Strategy affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 6) Promotion Effectiveness affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 7) Tourist Satisfaction affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 8) Destination Quality Integration influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction; 9) Pricing Strategy influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction; 10) Promotion Effectiveness influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction.

latest.title: “It Adds Flavor to It”: The Role of Code‐Switching in a Tourism Destination Chatbot
latest.abstract: Although code‐switching (the deliberate alternation between two languages) is well studied in advertising, its impact on chatbot interactions remains unexplored. Drawing on Communication Accommodation Theory, destination authenticity frameworks, and literature on code‐switching as a cultural positioning strategy, this mixed‐methods study investigates whether, and under which conditions, code‐switching into the destination language shapes chatbot evaluation, perceived destination brand authenticity and behavioral intentions. We conducted interviews (N = 16) and a between‐subjects experiment (N = 361, Portugal). Perceived communication accommodation was associated with higher chatbot evaluations, which in turn were associated with better perceptions of destination brand authenticity and behavioral intentions. Code‐switching activated the positive influence of cultural affinity on chatbot evaluation and behavioral intentions. This study offers one of the first empirical examinations of code‐switching in chatbot interactions from a marketing perspective. It corroborates and extends previous studies that advanced chatbot evaluation as an antecedent of perceived destination brand authenticity, and identifies code‐switching as an activator of latent cultural affinity effects, thereby advancing theoretical insights into linguistic cues in chatbots and providing practical guidelines for leveraging selective code‐switching to strengthen destination branding.

latest.title: USER-GENERATED CONTENT AND CUSTOMER PATRONAGE: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM SELECTED FOOD VENDORS IN BENIN CITY, NIGERIA
latest.venue: Ayden Journal of Management and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study examined the relationship between user-generated content (UGC) and customer patronage among selected food vendors in Benin City, Nigeria. Motivated by the critical role of user-generated content (UGC) in driving consumer trust, purchase behaviour, and brand loyalty within the food service sector, this study evaluated the specific effects of online customer reviews, ratings, testimonials, and social media engagement on customer patronage. Grounded in Social Proof Theory, Elaboration Likelihood Model, and Uses and Gratifications Theory, the study adopted cross-sectional survey design. The study population comprised customers of selected food vendors in Benin City who had recently interacted with online reviews, ratings, testimonials or social media content. Using Cochran's sample size formula and a purposive sampling technique, primary data were collected from 384 respondents via structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. The results indicated that the four UGC dimensions were jointly associated with customer patronage (R = .936, R2 = .875, F = 665.10, p < .05), accounting for 87.5% of the variance in customer patronage. Specifically, online customer reviews and ratings exhibited significant positive effects. Conversely, customer testimonials and social media engagement displayed significant negative effects. The findings suggest that unverified or poorly managed content can induce skepticism and reduce consumer confidence. The study concludes that user-generated narratives are pivotal drivers of patronage, but their efficacy depends greatly on authenticity and narrative control. Consequently, food vendors are advised to prioritise-service excellence to sustain high organic ratings, actively moderate onlin

latest.title: Work Overload, Job Satisfaction, and Employee Performance: The Mediating Role of Job Stress among Generation Z Employees in Semarang
latest.abstract: Background: Generation Z employees in Indonesia’s private sector may face demanding targets and irregular working hours. Evidence on how work overload and job satisfaction relate to performance and whether job stress mediates these relationships, remains inconsistent. Objective: This study analyses the effect of work overload and job satisfaction on employee performance, with job stress as an intervening variable, among Generation Z private-sector employees in Semarang City. Methods: An explanatory quantitative survey was conducted among 150 Generation Z employees aged 20–27 with at least two years of work experience, 86% of whom worked in production. Twenty-three indicators were measured on a five-point Likert scale and analysed with PLS-SEM using SmartPLS 4.0. Results: The estimated model yielded positive, statistically significant paths from work overload to job stress (β = 0.314) and performance (β = 0.445), and from job satisfaction to job stress (β = 0.613). The remaining direct paths and both indirect paths were nonsignificant. Four of six HTMT ratios exceeded 0.90, including 1.002 for job satisfaction and job stress. Conclusion: Discriminant validity was not established. The structural estimates are provisional and do not establish distinct construct-level relationships or rule out mediation.

latest.title: FROM STUDENT TO BRAND AMBASSADOR: THE ROLE OF INSTITUTIONAL BRANDING, SOCIAL MEDIA ENGAGEMENT, AND TRUST IN DEVELOPING STUDENT BRAND ADVOCACY
latest.venue: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)
latest.abstract: The higher education sector has become increasingly competitive, compelling universities to adopt innovative strategies to attract, engage, and retain students. In this environment, students are no longer viewed solely as recipients of educational services; they are increasingly recognized as influential stakeholders capable of shaping institutional reputation through positive word-of-mouth, peer recommendations, and social media interactions. Consequently, the concept of student brand advocacy has gained significant attention among higher education marketers and administrators. This conceptual paper explores how institutional branding, social media engagement, and trust contribute to the development of student brand advocacy. Drawing on Relationship Marketing Theory and Social Identity Theory, the paper proposes that a strong institutional brand fosters students' emotional connection and identification with their university. Similarly, active engagement through social media platforms strengthens communication and community participation, while trust reinforces students’ confidence in institutional values and performance. The paper further argues that student engagement acts as a central mechanism through which these factors encourage advocacy behaviour. By integrating branding, trust, and digital engagement into a unified framework, this study contributes to the growing literature on higher education marketing and student relationship management. The proposed framework offers practical insights for university leaders seeking to transform students into authentic brand ambassadors who actively contribute to institutional reputation and competitiveness.

latest.title: When Brands Matter Less: Perceived Product Similarity and Brand Switching Intention through Brand Relevance in Makassar's Grab-and-Go Coffee Market
latest.venue: Journal of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises
latest.abstract: Affordable grab-and-go coffee outlets in Makassar, Indonesia, increasingly sell comparable drinks at nearly identical prices, raising the question of whether brands still matter when products look alike. This study examines whether perceived product similarity increases brand switching intention by reducing brand relevance, that is, the importance consumers attach to brands when choosing within a category. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 250 consumers domiciled in Makassar who had a usual coffee brand and had tried at least one alternative in the same price range. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with 10,000 bootstrap subsamples. Perceived product similarity reduced brand relevance, and lower brand relevance increased brand switching intention. The resulting indirect effect of similarity on switching intention through brand relevance was positive and significant, whereas the direct effect was small and only marginally significant. The findings were robust to controlling for variety seeking, which influenced switching intention independently. The study shows that product similarity encourages switching mainly by weakening the role of the brand in consumers' choices rather than by acting on switching directly, which helps explain why earlier studies of brand parity and loyalty have reported inconsistent results. For small coffee businesses competing in a crowded price band, the results suggest that building distinctive reasons to choose the brand, such as a signature taste and consistent quality, is more effective for retaining customers than competing on price alone.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
