This not only provides suggestions for enterprises promoting green products and for governments wishing to raise environmental awareness via guidance and education but also promotes the sustainable development of green products.

hot.title: Role of Greenwashing in Influencing Brand Attitude and Consumption: Identifying Sustainable Business Strategies
hot.abstract: With firms' increasing adoption of green marketing strategies, greenwashing is also becoming more prevalent. Despite the negative consequences of greenwashing, limited studies have investigated its impact on attitude and consumption. Earlier studies have used greenwashing as a one‐dimensional construct and do not distinguish between different greenwashing practices. Based on the integrated framework of the Attribution Theory and the elaboration likelihood model, this study examines the effects of situational involvement with greenwashing practices on perceived greenwashing, green skepticism, and ultimately, brand attitude and purchase intention. Additionally, it investigates the moderating effect of environmental knowledge. Using a cross‐sectional research design, the study uses structural equation modeling to analyze the data collected from 353 US consumers. Findings suggest that greenwashing practices influence attitude and purchase intentions. The mediating role of green skepticism was also established. Additionally, the study highlights environmental knowledge's moderating role in the relationships studied. The results have implications for sustainable business practices and improving positive brand attitudes and green consumption by understanding customer perception of greenwashing.

hot.title: Leveraging social media for sustainable fashion: how brand and user-generated content influence Gen Z’s purchase intentions
hot.abstract: Purpose This study examines how brand-generated content (BGC) and user-generated content (UGC) on TikTok and Instagram shape Gen Z consumers’ purchase intentions for sustainable fashion. It also investigates the mediating role of social media engagement (SME) in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was employed, using stratified random sampling to target Gen Z consumers aged 16–28. Data were collected from 643 respondents through structured surveys and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Findings Both BGC and UGC positively influence purchase intentions, with BGC demonstrating a stronger effect due to its professional quality and emotional appeal. SME partially mediates these relationships, amplifying the impact of both content types on purchase behavior. Originality This research advances the sustainable fashion marketing literature by integrating insights from social media influence and consumer behavior, specifically within the Gen Z demographic. Unlike previous studies that focus solely on BGC or UGC in isolation, this study examines their interplay and the crucial mediating role of SME. The findings offer practical guidance for brands on how to strategically balance BGC and UGC to optimize consumer engagement and drive sustainable purchasing decisions.

hot.title: The Role of Organizational Culture in Digital Transformation and Modern Accounting Practices Among Jordanian SMEs
hot.venue: Journal of risk and financial management
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital transformation on modern accounting practices among Jordanian SMEs, focusing on the moderating role of organizational culture. Digital transformation using AI, blockchain, and cloud computing improves operational efficiency, real-time financial reporting, and decision making. However, the integration of these technologies poses challenges such as skill gaps, cost constraints, and cultural resistance. A quantitative survey of 480 employees in managerial roles from Jordanian SMEs shows that organizational culture plays a dual role as a driver and moderator of digital transformation. The findings confirm the role of digital transformation in reshaping modern accounting practices. Also, this study shows that to get the most out of digital transformation in accounting, a culture of innovation and continuous learning is required.

hot.title: Forty years of the theory of planned behavior: a bibliometric analysis (1985–2024)
hot.abstract: The goal of the study is a comprehensive and systematic analysis of the literature and research landscape of the TPB between 1985–2024. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric study of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) literature over the past forty years (1985–2024), analyzing 14,461 articles and 542,479 citations published in the Web of Science Core Collection. Utilizing performance analysis and science mapping techniques, the study leverages bibliographic coupling, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and a temporal assessment of the field across six distinct periods (1985–1999; 2000–2004, 2005–2009; 2010–2014; 2015–2019; and 2020–2024). Employing VOS Viewer software for visualization, this research maps the evolution, intellectual structure, and networks of relationships in the TPB field for the first time. The results highlight significant patterns and interdisciplinary connections, identifying the most influential publications, authors, journals, and institutions. A distinguishing feature of the study is the identification of thematic clusters based on multiple criteria and a triangulation analysis of these clusters. Additionally, the study investigates the most influential articles within the six periods and provides an evolutionary phase-wise analysis of TPB. Another highlight is the detailed guidance on future research avenues, which are actionable and based on a rigorous assessment of the most cited articles from 2020 to 2024. The study makes a significant contribution to the ongoing research conversations on the trajectory and growth of TPB across various disciplines.

hot.title: The impact of green HRM practices on green innovative work behaviour: empirical evidence from the hospitality sector of China and Pakistan
hot.abstract: Amid a global shift towards eco-friendly practices, this study investigates the impact of green human resource management (GHRM) practices on green innovative work behavior (GIWB) in the hospitality sector, focusing on emerging and developing countries, specifically China and Pakistan. The research also explores the mediating roles of green perceived organizational support (GPOS) and organizational citizenship behavior towards the environment (OCBE), as well as the moderating role of green transformational leadership (GTL). This study is grounded in the AMO (ability, motivation, and opportunity) theory and organizational support theory. Data were collected through a questionnaire, yielding 503 valid responses from hotel employees in Beijing, China, and 498 valid responses from Islamabad, Pakistan. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to examine and compare the results across both samples. The findings reveal positive and significant relationships between GHRM and GIWB, as well as notable mediation and moderation effects among the specified variables. Interestingly, GTL did not significantly moderate the relationship between GHRM and GIWB in Pakistan's sample, highlighting a regional contrast. This study contributes to advancing the implementation of GHRM practices to enhance GIWB in the hospitality sector, with insights into the role of GTL across different cultural contexts.

hot.title: Product reuse and repurpose in circular manufacturing: a critical review of key challenges, shortcomings and future directions
hot.abstract: This paper explores the transformative potential of reuse and repurposing strategies in the manufacturing industry, with a focus on sustainability and circular economy principles. Through an extensive review of 115 articles from Scopus using 6 different queries for broad topic coverage, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of reuse and repurposing frameworks, highlighting their benefits and challenges. The research identifies three essential pillars for successful implementation: product design, operational processes, and consumer acceptance. The study emphasizes the significance of modular designs, lifecycle extensions, and advanced cost models to maximize resource efficiency and sustainability. The paper also discusses the integration of advanced technologies, such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and IoT-enabled systems, to enhance traceability, streamline reverse logistics, and optimize predictive maintenance. Automated disassembly and collaborative robotics are highlighted as critical enablers for efficient and scalable reuse operations. Furthermore, the study advocates for flexible supply chains and real-time data analytics to address uncertainties in core acquisition and product variability. Despite the progress, the lack of standardized frameworks and metrics remains a significant barrier to widespread adoption. The paper concludes by proposing a cohesive framework that incorporates technological advancements, regulatory support, and collaborative approaches to overcome these limitations. This study provides actionable insights to foster a scalable, transparent, and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem.

hot.title: Green human resources management and green innovation: a meta-analytic review of strategic human resources levers for environmental sustainability
hot.abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has become a vital lever for driving organizational sustainability, yet the empirical relationship between GHRM and Green Innovation (GI) remains fragmented and inconclusive. This meta-analysis integrates findings from 52 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, encompassing 23,103 observations, to estimate the overall effect of GHRM on GI and to examine the influence of specific HR practices and contextual moderators. Grounded in the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study reveals a significant positive pooled effect, affirming that GHRM is a consistent and influential driver of GI. Among HR practices, green-linked compensation demonstrated the strongest impact, surpassing training and recruitment. Moderator analyses reveal that effect sizes differ meaningfully by industry type, firm size, and year of publication, but not by country development status or statistical method. These results contribute to theoretical advancement by integrating behavioral, strategic, and cognitive perspectives on sustainability-oriented innovation. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers on designing effective GHRM systems that stimulate eco-innovation. This study delivers the first quantitative synthesis clarifying when, where, and how GHRM enhances green innovation across diverse sectors and economies, providing a robust foundation for future research and strategy in sustainability-driven human capital development.

hot.title: The implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation for sustainability
hot.abstract: The interconnected phenomena of digital transformation and environmental innovation exert a major impact on sustainability . This research attempts to shed light on the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation. Both digital transformation and environmental innovation offer multiple opportunities to address global challenges such as climate change , resource depletion , and social inequality. This study highlights the need to integrate digital technologies and innovation with environmental initiatives. By following this approach, the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation can lead to a more resilient and sustainable society. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is used to determine the necessary or sufficient factors to increase sustainability. The study thus provides insights into what the environmental priorities should be. The results show how to reduce environmental impacts , improve quality of life , and support economic development. They can also be used to inform policies that support sustainability initiatives by encouraging the combinations of interventions that work best. By harnessing the potential of digital transformation and environmental innovation, it is possible to build a greener and more prosperous future for generations to come.

hot.title: Toward a Resilient and Sustainable Supply Chain: Operational Responses to Global Disruptions in the Post-COVID-19 Era
hot.abstract: Global supply chains have faced unprecedented disruptions in recent years, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to geopolitical tensions and climate-induced shocks. These events have exposed structural vulnerabilities in operational models overly optimized for efficiency at the expense of resilience and sustainability. This conceptual paper proposes an integrated framework linking resilience enablers, post-pandemic operational strategies, and sustainability outcomes. Through a synthesis of the interdisciplinary literature across operations management, sustainability science, institutional theory, and organizational behavior, we develop typologies of operational responses—including agile, lean–green, circular, and decentralized models—and connect them to broader Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on systems thinking and the Triple Bottom Line framework, we present a conceptual model that outlines causal relationships between resilience drivers, adaptive operational strategies, and long-term sustainable performance. The paper further discusses policy implications for public and private sectors, offering insights for global sustainability governance. We conclude by outlining a research agenda to empirically test and refine the model through multi-method approaches. This study contributes to theory by reconceptualizing sustainable operations in the context of compound global disruptions and offers a normative direction for future scholarship and practice.

hot.title: Closing the loop at the local scale: Investigating the drivers of and barriers to the implementation of the circular economy in cities and regions
hot.abstract: Transitioning to a circular economy (CE) at the local level is important for addressing the strain on natural resources caused by population growth and climate change. This study aims to investigate the factors that influence or impede the adoption of CE practices in French cities and regions. To achieve this goal, 47 interviews were conducted with practitioners from local authorities to identify the key elements that facilitate or hinder the implementation of CE. The findings highlight the crucial role of local authorities in enabling the transition to a CE, with critical support from political endorsement, strategic foresight, and effective leadership. However, obstacles such as organizational inertia, financial constraints, and a limited understanding of a CE present challenges to a CE's broader adoption. The study also emphasizes the critical role of partnerships and collaborative networks in overcoming these barriers and promoting the advancement of CE initiatives.

hot.title: Integrating Industry 4.0, Circular Economy, and Green HRM: A Framework for Sustainable Transformation
hot.abstract: The integration of Industry 4.0 technologies, Circular Economy (CE) principles, and Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) offers transformative potential to address global sustainability challenges. Industry 4.0, characterized by advanced digital technologies like IoT, Additive Manufacturing (AM), and Big Data Analytics (BDAA), enhances operational efficiency, resource optimization, and waste minimization. Concurrently, CE redefines economic models through resource conservation, lifecycle extension, and reduced environmental impact, supported by frameworks like ReSOLVE. GHRM aligns human resource practices with sustainability objectives, fostering Green behaviors and embedding environmental considerations into organizational culture. Despite the individual benefits of these frameworks, their combined application remains underexplored, with limited research on their systemic integration. This study addresses this gap by examining the synergies between Industry 4.0 technologies, CE principles, and GHRM strategies, identifying opportunities and challenges in their implementation. A theoretical model is proposed, emphasizing systemic innovation, resource efficiency, and collaborative value chains as key enablers of sustainable development. The model highlights the necessity of aligning technological advancements with human-centric approaches to overcome behavioral, organizational, and infrastructural barriers in transitioning toward sustainability. The findings offer practical insights for policymakers and industry leaders, outlining strategies for integrating Industry 4.0 with CE and GHRM to drive sustainability transitions. By synthesizing technological, environmental, and human resource dimensions, this research contributes both theoretically and practically, positionin

hot.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Factors for Sustainable Tourism Development: The Way Forward Toward Destination Resilience and Growth
hot.abstract: Although environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is increasingly gaining popularity in corporate and financial domains, its application in the tourism industry is still relatively underexplored. Hence, the objectives of this research are fivefold: (1) A systematic review appraises the extant literature on the intersection of the ESG dimensions and sustainable tourism; (2) It provides a synthesis of the content of the extracted articles and maps thematic intersections related to travel destinations' environmental stewardship, social equity and governance frameworks; (3) It assesses ESG‐aligned strategies that are intended to address the destinations' challenges including their carrying capacities and overtourism issues, climate risks, sociocultural tensions as well as institutional accountabilities; (4) It provides a holistic conceptual framework that guides policymakers, practitioners and stakeholders in integrating ESG into tourism planning and development, for sustainable and economically viable outcomes. In conclusion, (5) it advances theoretical and managerial implications.

hot.title: An investigation of determinants of green consumption behavior: An extended theory of planned behavior
hot.abstract: Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior , this research endeavors to delve into the multifarious determinants of green consumption behavior. It extends the traditional Theory of Planned Behavior framework by incorporating information intervention and social trust factors, constructing a comprehensive research model of green consumption behavior. Utilizing a robustly designed questionnaire, this study analyzed data from 354 collected samples using a quantitative research method . The findings revealed that: (1) green consumption attitude and perceived behavioral control significantly influenced green consumption intention, with perceived behavioral control exerting the strongest effect (P ​< ​0.001); (2) green consumption intention, location information, and social trust were significant predictors of green consumption behavior, with the intention being the most influential (P ​< ​0.001); (3) however, subjective norms, green advertising, and ecological labels did not significantly impact green consumption behavior (P ​> ​0.05). Based on these results, the study provides policy recommendations and marketing strategies to facilitate the promotion of green consumption practices.

hot.title: Fostering eco-friendly behaviors in hospitality: engaging customers through green practices, social influence, and personal dynamics
hot.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
hot.abstract: Purpose This study aims to delve into the intricate dynamics of customers’ pro-environmental behavior, examining the impact of external stimuli like hotel green practices (as contextual factors); internal stimuli, i.e. perceived consumer effectiveness, perceived environmental responsibility and pro-environmental self-identity (as individual factors); and social norms as social factors, on customers’ engagement in sustainable consumption (CEISC) and subsequent pro-environmental behaviors (PEBs). Design/methodology/approach An age-based quota sampling technique was used to gather data from customers visiting hotels in Pakistan. SmartPLS v.4 software was used to analyze the data, applying structural equation modeling and testing for the predictive powers of the model. Findings The results revealed the significant impact of both external and internal stimuli on customers’ PEBs, with higher impacts of hotel green practices and pro-environmental self-identity, underlining the complex nature of these influences. Results also revealed that social norms augment the influence of extrinsic and intrinsic factors on CEISC. Practical implications Hotels can enhance customer engagement by implementing green practices. In addition, leveraging social norms and tailoring communication strategies to highlight collective benefits can further amplify PEBs among guests. Originality/value This research provides a pioneering theoretical contribution by integrating the stimulus-organism-response model, the theory of planned behavior and the value-belief-norm theory in the realm of green consumerism in the hotel industry. It also addresses the potential gap linked to hotel green practices in leveraging customers’ PEBs in addition to their positive perceptions.

latest.title: Building socially responsible global brand identity with AI and sustainability strategy
latest.abstract: Purpose This research is an attempt to systematically review the current body of literature about strategic use of artificial intelligence and sustainability orientation to build a responsible global identity. Design/methodology/approach To conduct a systematic review and present a qualitative synthesis of literature, this research uses a multi-faceted four-stage PRISMA protocol that includes identification, screening, eligibility and inclusion. Findings Our analysis of academic knowledge reveals that available brand strategy literature mainly considers the consumer perspective and does not include the perspective of the global community of stakeholders. To address this gap, this study integrates sustainability orientation and AI strategy with governance, brand resilience and standardization–adaptation theory to explain how organizations can build socially responsible global brand identities. In doing so, the study provides a novel framework for balancing global consistency and local relevance in increasingly transparent and digitally connected markets. Originality/value This research offers a comprehensive analysis of theoretical, methodological and empirical knowledge to find answers to the research questions raised by the current context of sustainability consciousness and new age of artificial technologies.

latest.title: Exploring digital brand personality through logo design: Insights for Thai and Burmese
latest.venue: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences Studies
latest.abstract: When a logo is created with brand personality, this mere visual symbol becomes alive. It enhances the effectiveness of numerous branding strategies and the competitive advantage of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the digital markets. However, existing studies focusing on logo development and brand personality using the three elements—color, shape, and typeface are limited. This study conducted a quantitative online survey with 122 participants (62 Thais and 60 Burmese) aged 18 to 44 years. It aims to 1) study brand personality perceptions towards digital logos designed with color, shape, and typeface and 2) conduct a comparative study of logo design preferences between Thai and Burmese consumers. The findings revealed that 1) some logos conveyed several brand personality dimensions rather than one expected dimension and 2) both Thai and Burmese consumers preferred logo designs similarly. The logo designs that included light colors—green, pink, and white—together with organic shapes and display typefaces were associated with all brand personality dimensions and were also strongly preferred by the participants. This study extends brand personality literature through novel cross-cultural insights from Thailand and Myanmar while providing guidelines to practitioners on how to design logos with suitable brand personality in these emerging markets.

latest.title: When luxury becomes too common: How democratization triggers love-becomes-hate through embarrassment and betrayal
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: This study investigates how luxury democratization damages consumer–brand relationships through emotional and relational mechanisms. Although prior research has examined reduced exclusivity, value decline, and purchase intentions, the underlying psychological mechanisms remain underexplored. Drawing on self-conscious emotion theory, expectancy violation theory, and a relationship breakdown perspective, this research proposes that luxury democratization initiates a staged deterioration process. A two-study design is employed. Study 1 used a scenario-based experiment to test causal and sequential mediation effects. Study 2 used a survey-based approach with partial least squares structural equation modeling to examine the full framework, including behavioral outcomes and moderating effects, and applied combined importance–performance map analysis (cIPMA) to identify managerial priorities. Findings show that luxury democratization increases brand embarrassment, which leads to perceived betrayal and love-becomes-hate; this emotional reversal further increases desire to punish the brand. Luxury brand attachment strengthens the betrayal–love-becomes-hate relationship but weakens the betrayal–punishment relationship. The study contributes by showing that democratization creates relational deterioration, not only evaluative decline, and offers tactics for monitoring embarrassment and mitigating betrayal. As the data were collected from Chinese online respondents and rely on scenario-based and survey measures, future research should test high-spending consumers or private-client groups, use longitudinal or behavioral data, compare different democratization forms, and examine alternative emotional pathways.

latest.title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
latest.abstract: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

latest.title: From Counter-Cultural Branding to Symbolic Cultural Influence: Apple, Symbolic Consumption, and Hyperreal Lifestyle as a Theoretical Lens
latest.venue: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study critically examines the cultural significance of Apple Inc. by exploring how its technological products and brand representations acquire meanings related to creativity, identity, status, and lifestyle beyond their functional utility. Drawing on Gramscian cultural hegemony, Cultural Studies, Baudrillard's concepts of simulacra and hyperreality, and Castells' Network Society, the study provides a theoretically informed interpretation of Apple's cultural positioning and symbolic consumption. Particular attention is given to the Diderot Effect within Apple's ecosystem, through which complementary products may acquire functional and symbolic meaning through interconnected consumption. Drawing on qualitative interpretations of selected advertising campaigns and source-specific secondary evidence on iPhone consumption, ecosystem participation, generational indicators, and social-digital interaction, the study interprets Apple's cultural influence through the interaction of functional value, symbolic consumption, ecosystem participation, and social meaning. The analysis suggests that Apple-related products may function simultaneously as technologically useful objects and symbolic resources within particular consumer and social contexts. Cultural hegemony, symbolic consumption, networked identity, and hyperreality are therefore employed as complementary theoretical lenses rather than as empirically demonstrated mechanisms.

latest.title: The Effect of Customer Experience on Purchase Intention in Indonesian E-Commerce: Mediating Effect of Brand Trust
latest.abstract: Rapid digitalization has intensified e-commerce competition in Indonesia, highlighting the importance of customer experience and brand trust in shaping consumers’ purchase intentions. This study examines whether brand trust mediates the relationship between customer experience and purchase intention among Indonesian e-commerce users. Drawing on Stimulus–Organism–Response theory and relationship marketing theory, the study conceptualizes customer experience as the stimulus, brand trust as the psychological mechanism, and purchase intention as the behavioral response. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 280 active e-commerce users who had made at least one online purchase during the previous six months. Data were collected using a structured five-point Likert questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that customer experience has a positive and significant relationship with purchase intention, customer experience positively relates to brand trust, and brand trust positively relates to purchase intention. The indirect effect indicates partial mediation. The findings suggest that positive digital experiences can strengthen trust, which in turn is associated with stronger purchase intentions. The study contributes context-specific evidence from Indonesian e-commerce and clarifies the process through which experience is linked to purchase intention.

latest.title: Perceived Sustainability Marketing Influences Customer Loyalty: The Moderating Effect of Customer Environmental Concern
latest.abstract: Sustainability marketing has become a major strategy for building consumer loyalty, particularly in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). This study examines how consumer-perceived sustainability marketing affects loyalty toward culinary MSMEs in Ambon City and whether consumer environmental concern moderates this relationship. A quantitative cross-sectional survey involved 180 consumers of culinary MSMEs. Data were analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS version 4. Consumer-perceived sustainability marketing had a positive and significant effect on consumer loyalty (β = 0.577; t = 8.547; p < 0.001). Consumer environmental concern significantly strengthened this relationship (β = 0.094; t = 2.022; p = 0.043). The results suggest that sustainability marketing can build loyalty when its messages align with consumers’ environmental values. Culinary MSMEs can encourage loyalty by communicating sustainable practices consistently and considering consumers’ environmental interests. The study contributes a consumer-perception perspective to sustainability marketing research and identifies environmental concern as a contingency factor in consumer loyalty.

latest.title: The impact of Generative AI chatbots on behavioral intention in travel planning: A theory of consumption value perspective
latest.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots are revolutionizing online travel planning by transitioning travelers' focus from merely gathering information to obtaining personalized recommendations and facilitating seamless bookings. Grounded in the Interactive Technology Acceptance Model and Consumption Value Theory, this study investigates how the attributes of GenAI chatbots, specifically personalization and anthropomorphism, alongside user traits such as self-efficacy and personal innovativeness, influence travel planning intention through perceived value. Data collected from a questionnaire survey were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that GenAI chatbot attributes (personalization and anthropomorphism) and user traits (self-efficacy and personal innovativeness) exert significant direct positive effects on perceived values. The indirect effects of anthropomorphism, personalization, self-efficacy, and personal innovativeness on adoption intentions are most pronounced through hedonic value, followed by utilitarian value, with novelty value playing the least prominent mediating role. This study enriches the theoretical understanding of AI-based customer service and provides tourism businesses with insights into enhancing GenAI's features and shaping consumer perceptions.

latest.title: Digital Transformation Adoption Requirements as a Strategic Option in Business Organizations
latest.abstract: This study explores digital transformation as a strategic option capable of fundamentally changing an organization’s structure and way of operating, rather than treating it merely as technology or a set of technological systems. Drawing on a review of the literature, the paper focuses on the complex and interconnected nature of this transformation, which spans several dimensions: the technological dimension, associated with developing technical infrastructure; the organizational dimension, concerned with restructuring administrative processes; the cultural dimension, involving changes in mindsets and work practices; and the strategic dimension, which entails revising long-term visions and objectives. The paper examines the opportunities offered by digital transformation, including improving operational efficiency by accelerating processes and increasing productivity, innovating business models that create distinctive value in a challenging marketplace, and enhancing customer experience by making interactions between organizations and customers more responsive and better tailored to individual needs. It also addresses major barriers to transformation, ranging from resistance to change and shortages of digital skills to administrative constraints that impede effective implementation of strategic decisions.

latest.title: The Mediating Effect of Brand Trust in the Relationship Between Customer Experience and Repurchase Intention
latest.abstract: Digital technology has transformed consumer purchasing behavior through e-commerce platforms such as Shopee. However, the inability to physically examine products makes customer experience and brand trust essential in encouraging repurchase intention. This study aims to examine the effect of customer experience on repurchase intention, with brand trust serving as a mediating variable, among consumers of SAFF & Co. products purchased through Shopee in Denpasar, Indonesia. A quantitative, explanatory research design was employed through a cross-sectional survey. Data from 110 purposively sampled respondents were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS. Results indicate that customer experience positively influences repurchase intention (β = 0.485, t = 3.561, p < 0.001) and brand trust (β = 0.643, t = 7.683, p < 0.001). Brand trust also has a significant positive effect on repurchase intention (β = 0.422, t = 2.610, p = 0.005) and mediates the relationship between customer experience and repurchase intention (indirect effect = 0.271, t = 2.558, p = 0.005). The findings highlight the importance of enhancing customer experience and building brand trust to foster repurchase intention in e-commerce settings. Practical implications for SAFF & Co. involve improving customer interactions throughout the online purchasing journey.

latest.title: Understanding Social Media Marketing and Consumer Preferences: Study of Stationery Brand in Indian Market
latest.abstract: The evolution of digital technologies has significantly transformed marketing and created new ways for businesses to communicate with consumers. Marketing through social media platforms, influencer marketing, optimising through search engines, content creation and online advertising are commonly used marketing strategies. Within the stationery market of India, a variety of products are being sold such as; notebooks, pens, pencils, art stationery, office stationery and school stationery. Consumers are able to view stationery brands on digital platforms to compare features of the products. Consumers are also able to observe the products and give feedback. This research aims to look at the relationships between social media marketing, and awareness, preference and engagement with stationery brands. It will take into consideration how consumers react to social media, value of how products are displayed digitally, brand awareness and consumer engagement through digital platforms. A descriptive research method has been used and primary data was collated via a well-structured questionnaire. Secondary data was also collated from suitable resources. Social media marketing, influencer marketing, search engine optimisation, content and advertisement are common marketing methods. In the Indian market for stationery, many products are available including. Notebooks, pens, pencils, artistic stationery, office stationery and school stationery. Consumers can research stationery brands on digital platforms and compare the features. They can also view the products and provide feedback. This research looks to understand the relationship between social media marketing, brand awareness, brand preference and brand engagement within stationery brands. latest.title: Driving E-Loyalty in Live-Streaming Commerce: Roles of Platform Interactivity, Streamer Attractiveness, and Customer Engagement
latest.abstract: The growing adoption of TikTok live-streaming commerce does not necessarily translate into sustained e-loyalty, highlighting the need to understand the mechanisms underlying loyalty formation. This study examines the effects of platform interactivity and physical attractiveness on e-loyalty and the mediating role of customer engagement among Glad2Glow customers in Padang City. Data were collected through a quantitative survey of 200 customers who had purchased Glad2Glow products through TikTok live streaming at least twice in the previous six months and analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4.0. The results show that platform interactivity positively affects customer engagement (t = 3.976, p < 0.000) and e-loyalty (t = 2.989, p = 0.003). Physical attractiveness positively affects customer engagement (t = 2.683, p = 0.007) but does not directly affect e-loyalty (t = 0.959, p = 0.338). Customer engagement positively affects e-loyalty (t = 5.715, p < 0.000) and mediates the relationships of platform interactivity (t = 3.114, p = 0.002) and physical attractiveness (t = 2.446, p = 0.014) with e-loyalty. These findings highlight customer engagement as a key mechanism in e-loyalty formation and suggest that firms should prioritize interactive communication and customer engagement rather than relying solely on visual attractiveness. The study extends the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework in live-streaming commerce.

latest.title: Brand Awareness and Brand Image Shape Purchase Intention through Brand Trust in Indonesia’s Fresh Food E-Commerce Market
latest.abstract: Fresh food e-commerce expanded sharply in Indonesia, yet it remains unclear whether the brand knowledge platforms accumulated under mobility restrictions still convert into purchase intention now that the market has normalized. This study examines the effect of brand awareness and brand image on purchase intention and tests brand trust as a mediator, using Sayurbox as the empirical setting. An online questionnaire produced 176 purposively sampled responses from urban Indonesian consumers, analyzed using PLS-SEM. Brand awareness (t = 2.044, p = 0.041) and brand image (t = 2.257, p = 0.024) significantly affect purchase intention and brand trust (t = 4.174, p < 0.001; t = 2.899, p = 0.004). Brand trust is the strongest determinant of purchase intention (t = 3.215, p = 0.001) and partially mediates both paths (p = 0.006; p = 0.037), and it is built more by familiarity than by image. For fresh food platforms, staying top of mind and delivering reliably are therefore the levers that turn brand knowledge into purchase: consistent visibility, freshness guarantees, on-time delivery, and prompt replacement of damaged items build the trust that drives intention. Platforms outgrowing the category in their name should broaden their brand associations before widening the assortment.

latest.title: Social Media Content’s Effect On Customer Loyalty Building
latest.abstract: Social media has become a way for businesses to connect with the public and build a strong base of regular customers. Social media advertising can continuously speak with the public, personalise messages for different groups, and invite them to participate in the campaign. The quality, relevance, authenticity and interactivity of social media content can affect consumers' perceptions, brand trust, emotional attachment and repeat-purchase behaviour. Research on the impact of social media content on customer loyalty: Theoretical basis, characteristics of good content and applications of online communication in customer relationship building. Develop all sorts of practical content strategies, such as educational posts, interactive activities, user-generated content, personalised communication, etc. Pay attention to the problems of information overload, misleading messages, privacy concerns and inconsistent brand communication. Papers have provided some practical ways to plan content, attract customers and measure results. Therefore, it can be concluded that if enterprises offer high-quality information, ensure the reliability of communication, and provide good services in the digital environment, social media can attract and retain consumers over time.

latest.title: PENGARUH INFLUENCER MARKETING DAN EMOTIONAL BRANDING TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN GENERASI Z DI TOMORO COFFEE KOTA MEDAN
latest.venue: Didaktik Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang
latest.abstract: The growth of social media has changed how Generation Z seeks information and makes purchase decisions, including in the increasingly competitive coffee shop industry. Previous findings on the effects of influencer marketing and emotional branding on purchase decisions remain inconsistent. This study examines the partial and simultaneous effects of both variables on Generation Z’s purchase decisions at Tomoro Coffee in Medan City. A quantitative associative design was used, with primary data collected through a five-point Likert questionnaire completed by 100 respondents aged 18–29 years selected by purposive sampling (February–April 2026). The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS. The results show that influencer marketing (B = 0.334; p < 0.001) and emotional branding (B = 0.461; p < 0.001) each have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, and that both have a significant simultaneous effect (F = 115.478; p < 0.001). The adjusted R² of 0.698 indicates that the two variables explain 69.8% of the variance in purchase decisions. The contributions of the two variables are relatively similar, with emotional branding slightly larger. These findings suggest that coffee shop managers should combine credible and relevant influencer collaborations with stronger emotional brand attachment.

latest.title: Konstruksi Citra Konsumen Etis Melalui Representasi Nilai Keberlanjutan (Studi pada Website Merek Fashion Armedangels)
latest.abstract: This article discusses how sustainability discourse in the fashion industry is used to shape consumer identity through digital media. The research focuses on the content available on the official website of the German fashion brand Armedangels, explaining how visual and textual elements on the website work to construct the myth of the ethical consumer within German society, which has a high level of environmental awareness (Umweltbewusstsein). Using a qualitative approach, this study applies Roland Barthes' semiotic analysis at the levels of denotation, connotation, and myth. Using a qualitative approach, this study applies Roland Barthes' semiotic analysis at the levels of denotation, connotation, and myth. The results of the study show that Armedangels uses digital communication such as information on organic raw materials, water efficiency, circular technology, and official certifications as a tool to touch the psychological side of consumers. These signs work by managing consumer guilt related to environmental issues into a motivation that transforms consumption activities into a form of social responsibility, thereby shaping the image of the ethical consumer as a new lifestyle standard in modern German society. Abstrak Artikel ini membahas tentang wacana keberlanjutan dalam industri fashion digunakan untuk membentuk identitas konsumen melalui media digital. Fokus penelitian dilakukan terhadap materi yang ada pada website resmi merek fashion asal Jerman, yaitu Armedangels, dengan menjelaskan bagaimana elemen visual dan teks pada website tersebut bekerja dalam mengonstruksi mitos konsumen etis di tengah masyarakat Jerman yang memiliki kesadaran akan lingkungan (Umweltbewusstsein) yang tinggi. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif, penelitian ini menerapkan analisi

latest.title: Conceptualising brand purpose as a multidimensional marketing and management construct: a qualitative framework
latest.abstract: Brand purpose has been explored across organisational, stakeholder, authenticity, sustainability and brand-equity research but remains difficult to define consistently. This paper aims to create a combined multidimensional model of brand purpose and create an initial set of items for further validation. By conducting a concept-based literature review we identified eleven tentative domains. Through an iterative two-round expert consultation process these domains were questioned and adjusted. We used a combination of deductive-inductive and grounded theory coding techniques when analysing the data from our 15-member panel of experts (made up of both academics and practitioners). An additional expert panel of 11 provided written input which was used to inform initial item creation. As the focus of the expert round was to challenge and improve upon our domains, this should not be considered validation of the items. Our domains can be grouped into four themes: a beyond-profit core, internal embedding, stakeholder experience, and impact and brand outcomes. Theoretically, our paper integrates these domains and clarifies boundaries between similar concepts. Managerially, it provides a structured basis for reflecting on brand purpose. Lastly, we created a set of items that require future validation.

latest.title: Exploring the relationship between consumer religiosity and perceptions of corporate social responsibility in tobacco companies: Does smoking status matter?
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has become an essential component of corporate strategy, aiming at improving social and environmental outcomes. It is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for shaping public perceptions of businesses' fair treatment of employees and consumers, addressing social issues, profit orientation, and overall commitment to ethical practices. However, controversial industries are frequently accused of exploiting CSR initiatives. These range from the core “sin” sectors of tobacco, alcohol, and gambling to more contested categories such as fast food and fossil fuels. Such firms often establish their own permissive guidelines under the guise of social responsibility, potentially undermining genuine efforts for positive change. Tobacco, the most consistently classified sin industry, provides the focal context for this study. This study examines how different types of religiosity affect consumers' views on tobacco companies' CSR and their support for these companies, with consumer corporate identity (CCI) serving as a mediator. It also explores how smoking status moderates the relationship between religiosity and CCI. Design/methodology/approach Using a survey of consumers in Indonesia (n = 331), our findings reveal a complex relationship between consumers' religiosity, smoking status, and their perceptions of tobacco companies. Findings Intrinsic religiosity positively shaped CSR perceptions across four of five domains: employee, social, profit, and ethics, with no significant effect on consumer-focused initiatives. Smokers who are more likely to identify with tobacco companies were more inclined to support the CSR initiatives, even disregarding their detrimental effects on society. Extrinsically religious people also show a positiv

latest.title: Dimensions of Brand Activism as Predictors of Customer Purchase Intention: A Study of Multinational Brands in Nigeria
latest.abstract: The research evaluated the effect of brand activism on customer purchase intention toward multinational companies’ products in South-West Nigeria. The research adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. The study's population was limited to customers of multinational companies in South-West Nigeria. The sample size of 384 participants was selected for the study. It was determined using the Cochran formula. The study used the judgmental sampling technique. The data for this study were generated from the primary source through the use of a structured questionnaire. The study used internal consistency reliability. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques in order to arrive at a conclusion. The findings revealed that value-driven communications have a positive and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = 0.139, p < 0.05), indicating that ethical and value-based messaging can influence consumers, though with a relatively modest impact. Brand authenticity emerged as the strongest predictor of customer purchase intention (β = 0.721, p < 0.05), underscoring the critical role of perceived sincerity, consistency, and credibility in shaping consumer trust and emotional attachment. In contrast, woke-washing was found to have a negative and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = −0.080, p < 0.05), suggesting that consumers penalize brands perceived to engage in superficial or insincere activism. The study concludes that while value-driven communications are important, authentic and consistent brand activism is far more influential in driving purchase intentions, whereas woke-washing undermines trust and weakens brand–consumer relationships. It therefore recommends that multinational companies align activism mess

latest.title: Decoding Youth Event Attendance Intention on Instagram: A Funnel Perspective On Content Formats and Attributes
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
latest.abstract: In the modern landscape of experiential entertainment, social media- predominantly Instagram- has cemented itself as the final commonplace view-point for event discovery, engagement, and decision-making. Basing off the applied insights garnered from the end-to-end experience at Wild High Nights- an artist management, entertainment, and live events company in Kerala- this paper analyses the observable influence of different categories of Instagram content- Reels, Stories, static posts, and atmosphere videos; versus different content dimensions- entertainment, event logistics, artist appeal, and social proof- on the consumers' expressed intent to attend live events and concerts. Using a descriptive quantitative research approach through the empirical survey of a sample of 100 active Instagram users and event goers, this paper seeks to explore the data-inconsistency between vanity metrics at the top-of-the- orifice (views and reach) vis-à-vis the desired bottom-of-the-orifice action (attendance). Findings identify short-form video (Reels) as the format of choice for front-end attention (38% preference) closely followed by event- atmosphere videos (27%), interactive Stories (20%), and static Posts (15%). While entertainment (82%) and artists (71%) attract the initial platform interest, it is the perceived behavioral control, precisely the clarity in event-related information- dates, venues, timings, and ticketing- that triggers actual attendance (76%). Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior and the Stimulus-Organism-Response model, an integrated content-funnel is proposed, along with practical recommendations for independent promoters to effectively reallocate their digital marketing budget and induce higher box-office sales.

latest.title: Post-Purchase Ambivalent Attitude Change: From Double to Triple Induced/Forced Compliance
latest.abstract: Post-purchase cognitive dissonance may arise following high-involvement purchases when consumers simultaneously hold favorable and unfavorable evaluations of the purchased product. Although the Double Induced/Forced Compliance Paradigm explains cumulative dissonance through two successive high-commitment counter-attitudinal behaviors, whether extending the behavioral sequence beyond two behaviors can provide further repetition relevant to durable attitude change remains unresolved. This conceptual study develops the Triple Induced/Forced Compliance Paradigm to address this gap in naturalistic high-involvement post-purchase contexts. The study adopts a theory-constrained conceptual development approach that identifies the conceptual gap, integrates relevant theoretical perspectives, and formulates theoretically grounded propositions linking initial attitude, successive customer behaviors, and customer–brand relational conditions. The framework specifies an ego-involved, highly stable, and resistant ambivalent post-purchase attitude as the initial condition and three successive high-commitment counter-attitudinal behaviors: brand community participation, brand recommendation, and publicizing, supported by customer brand identification, customer brand trust, and customer brand loyalty. The conceptual findings indicate that these three behaviors form a cumulative sequence through which cognitive dissonance progressively accumulates, with subsequent attitude change theorized to reduce the accumulated dissonance. Managerially, the framework suggests treating these behaviors as a connected post-purchase sequence supporting more positive consumer attitudes and sustained consumer–brand engagement.

latest.title: Perceived Brand Authenticity, Perceived Quality, and Repurchase Intention: Comparative Evidence from CHAGEE and TEAZZI Consumers
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Business and Entrepreneurship Research
latest.abstract: This study examined whether perceived brand authenticity and perceived quality were associated with repurchase intention among CHAGEE and TEAZZI consumers and whether these associations differed between brands. A cross-sectional survey included 107 purposively selected consumers in Surabaya, Indonesia (54 CHAGEE and 53 TEAZZI). Brand-specific multiple regressions, Welch's independent-samples tests, and pooled regression with brand interactions and HC3 robust standard errors were used. Perceived brand authenticity was positively associated with repurchase intention for TEAZZI (B = 0.554, p < 0.001) and CHAGEE (B = 0.511, p = 0.002). Perceived quality showed corresponding positive associations for TEAZZI (B = 0.440, p = 0.002) and CHAGEE (B = 0.344, p = 0.0497); the CHAGEE estimate requires particular caution. The mean comparisons and brand-interaction tests were not statistically significant, although they did not establish equivalence between brands. Internal-consistency estimates ranged from 0.554 to 0.754, and the modest, nonprobability sample limits measurement confidence and comparative precision. The study offers exploratory evidence that symbolic evaluations of brand identity and functional assessments of product quality are each associated with stated repurchase intention, while distinguishing differences in average evaluations from differences in regression relationships. The cross-sectional findings do not support causal claims or direct conclusions about actual repeat purchasing.

latest.title: Driving gratification and platform retention in Thailand’s Generation Z creator journey
latest.abstract: Grounded in Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT), this study tests a conceptual framework examining how intrinsic (self-expression, entertainment) and extrinsic (social enhancement, monetization) motivations shape perceived gratification and, subsequently, Generation Z creators’ intention to continue producing non-sponsored user-generated content. Quantitative data were collected via a cross-sectional survey of 364 Thai Generation Z social media users, who actively post non-sponsored content at least once per week. Following measurement model validation through Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) in IBM SPSS AMOS, path analysis using Hayes’ PROCESS Macro (Model 4) in IBM SPSS revealed that entertainment value emerges as the primary determinant of perceived gratification, followed by social enhancement, and self-expression. Surprisingly, perceived gratification does not directly impact intention to continue with content creation on the platform, nor does it mediate the relationship between the motivators and creators’ continuance intention on the platform. Instead, three antecedent motivators directly drive continuation intentions, with monetization emerging as the strongest driver, followed by entertainment value, and social enhancement. These findings suggest that maximizing Generation Z creator retention requires platform managers and brand marketers to offer an evolving incentive structure: maintaining core entertainment and social enhancement rewards while transitioning creators from initial self-expression to transparent monetization.

latest.title: Building a Marketing-Effect Index as a Decision-Support Tool for SME Cross-Border Floral Trade
latest.abstract: This study developed a pragmatic effectiveness index to evaluate cross-border e-commerce language strategies for floral businesses. This research was conducted because flowers face a trust gap in global logistics, and traditional literal translation fails to meet the cultural and emotional needs of overseas consumers, resulting in low sales. To address this, an empirical A/B test was conducted over 30 days on an e-commerce platform, comparing traditional descriptions with artificial intelligence-assisted, manually calibrated copy optimized for emotional density and pragmatic trust. The experiment revealed that the optimized copy increased the conversion rate by nearly six times and reduced the refund rate from 8.4% to 3.2%. Ultimately, these findings signify that brand promotion must dynamically balance aesthetic appeal with pragmatic trust, providing a quantitative paradigm to help agricultural exports overcome cultural discounts and achieve higher conversion.

latest.title: Study on the Influence of Coaching Leadership Styles on Sports Training Willingness
latest.venue: Journal of Educational Development and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Coaching leadership style is an important social influence factor in sports contexts, directly affecting athletes' training motivation, persistence, and competitive performance. Based on leadership behavior theory and self-determination theory, this study employs literature analysis, questionnaire surveys, and statistical methods to investigate the impact mechanisms of transformational, transactional, and laissez-faire leadership on athletes’ training willingness, using provincial and university team athletes as research subjects. The Sport Leadership Behavior Scale and Training Willingness Scale were used to collect data, while also examining the mediating roles of basic psychological needs and training satisfaction. Results show that transformational leadership significantly predicts training willingness positively, with personalized care and intellectual stimulation playing key roles. Contingent reward and active exception management within transactional leadership also have positive effects on training willingness, whereas negative exception management and laissez-faire leadership negatively affect it. Satisfaction of autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs partially mediates the relationship between transformational leadership and training willingness, while training satisfaction fully mediates the relationship between transactional leadership and training willingness. Therefore, coaches are advised to strengthen transformational leadership behaviors during training by providing individualized feedback, setting goals, appropriately applying rewards, and creating a supportive environment that fosters athlete autonomy, thereby enhancing both training motivation and performance. The findings offer practical guidance for improving coaching leadership styles and man

latest.title: PLAYING THE PAST: GAMIFICATION AS A STRATEGIC INSTRUMENT IN CULTURAL HERITAGE MARKETING AND BRAND BUILDING
latest.venue: Journal of Ancient History and Archeology
latest.abstract: Cultural heritage institutions and destinations operate in an attention economy, competing less with one another than with streaming platforms, mobile games and social media for discretionary time. Gamification, understood as the use of game design elements in non-game contexts, has been widely studied in heritage as a learning and engagement device, but far less as a marketing and branding instrument. This paper addresses that gap. Drawing on gamification theory, self-determination theory and customer-based brand equity, it develops the Play-to-Brand framework, linking four groups of game mechanics (progression, social, narrative and spatial-discovery) to brand equity outcomes (awareness, associations and imagery, perceived quality, and resonance/loyalty), moderated by mechanic-meaning fit, audience readiness and technological affordance. The framework is illustrated and refined through a comparative analysis of five European heritage gamification initiatives spanning museum-published video games, research-led locative games, in-gallery companion games, destination-scale collection programmes and unplanned platform spillover, alongside a Bulgarian comparator used to examine analogue gamification under less favourable conditions. The analysis identifies branding mechanisms (reach extension, brand personality repositioning, co-created narratives, behavioural data, and mechanic-driven repeat visitation) and risks (authenticity dilution, pointsification, dissonance, and lifecycle abandonment). The paper concludes by proposing design principles, a measurement framework for practitioners, and a future research agenda.

latest.title: Role of Digital Video Advertisement Performance and Image Congruity in Building Brand Respect and Brand Love in the Hospitality Context: Chinese Customers’ Perspectives
latest.abstract: This study investigated how digital video advertisement performance factors – informativeness, entertainment, interactivity, innovativeness, and proactiveness – affect the development of brand respect and brand love in the hospitality context. Building on self-congruity and lovemark theories, the study tested the links between these advertising performance factors, two forms of image congruity (ideal image and ideal social image), and consumer responses in terms of brand respect and brand love. The results indicate that all dimensions played essential roles, highlighting the importance of both personal and social congruity in strengthening emotional brand attachment. In addition, hospitality product type (hotel versus restaurant) was found to moderate these relationships. Using structural equation modeling (SEM), necessary condition analysis, and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), the research identified multiple causal pathways leading to strong consumer–brand relationships without a single necessary condition. The findings guide hospitality marketers to design emotionally resonant and interactive advertising strategies. The findings also extend existing theories on congruity-driven branding in the context of digital video advertisements. This study has valuable academic and practical implications.

latest.title: From Environmental Knowledge to Green Flight Preference: An Empirical Study
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: The growing emphasis on environmental sustainability has intensified the need to understand sustainable consumer behaviour in the airline industry. This study develops and tests an integrated model examining the relationships between perceived environmental knowledge, green marketing awareness, green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Data were collected from airline passengers in Türkiye and analysed using a structural equation modelling approach. The findings indicate that perceived environmental knowledge positively influences both green marketing awareness and green flight preference, while its effect on green brand trust is not significant and its relationship with price tolerance is negative. Green marketing awareness positively affects green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Green brand trust does not play a positive moderating role in the effect of green marketing awareness on green flight preference. In addition, green brand trust significantly enhances green flight preference. The results suggest that environmental knowledge alone is insufficient to foster price acceptance for green flight options, highlighting the importance of credible green marketing practices in shaping trust and behavioural intentions in the airline industry. The study contributes to sustainable consumer behaviour literature by integrating cognitive, marketing and behavioural constructs in aviation context.

latest.title: A meta-analytic synthesis of brand love: Investigating the moderating role of culture
Customer Engagement towards Loyalty in the context of Influencer Marketing that Leads an Organization’s Resilience in Digital Ecosystems – A Theoretical Perspective
latest.abstract: Influencer marketing has risen from an experimental tactic to a relationship-building mechanism, which is interconnected with digital ecosystems. Influencers are largely used by brands to earn likes, comments and shares, yet this attention span is often very less. This conceptual paper raises the questions as how short-term engagement can convert to customer loyalty, and the contribution of loyalty to enterprise resilience. This study proposes the three-stage framework and ten propositions for integrating the credibility at source level, trust- commitment, customer engagement and dynamic capabilities perspectives. Influencer credibility, authenticity, para social interaction, content relevance and influencer–brand congruence are drivers of engagement; brand trust, commitment and attachment conversion are proposed as mechanisms that convert engagement into brand loyalty, wherein it strengthens the resilience subject to influencer and platform dependency and to ecosystem synergy and turbulence. The observations in this paper links consumer-level relationship outcomes with enterprise-level capabilities, offers propositions for empirical testing drawing managerial implications for sustainable and relationship-centred digital strategies.

latest.title: From Virtual to Valuable: How Influencer Type and Product Type Shape Consumer Value Co‐Creation Intention
latest.abstract: Virtual and human influencers offer distinct social and experiential cues, but their relative effectiveness may depend on how consumers evaluate the endorsed product. Drawing on the cognitive‐affective‐behavioral framework, this research integrates social information processing theory and cognitive‐affective system theory to examine consumer value co‐creation intention. Across three between‐subjects experiments (N = 994), results reveal a consistent matching effect: virtual influencers have a relative advantage for search products, whereas human influencers have a relative advantage for experience products. This matching effect operates through parasocial interaction and empathy: forming a parasocial representation may make an influencer's perspective and affective cues more accessible, providing a relational basis for subsequent empathy. Consistent with this sequence, both the indirect effect through parasocial interaction and the serial indirect effect through parasocial interaction and empathy follow this product‐dependent pattern across both product categories, whereas the indirect effect through empathy alone favors human influencers only for experience products. Together, these findings identify product type as a boundary condition linking relational and affective processes to consumer value co‐creation intention, offering practical insights for aligning influencer selection with product characteristics.

latest.title: A ADAPTAÇÃO CULTURAL DAS MARCAS NA PUBLICIDADE CONTEMPORÂNEA: ESTRATÉGIAS DE COMUNICAÇÃO E PERTENCIMENTO CULTURAL
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: Contemporary advertising has adopted cultural adaptation strategies to strengthen the connection between brands and consumers in different social and cultural contexts. In this way, companies adapt visual and communicational elements of their campaigns to engage with local traditions, beliefs, and identities. This article analyzes how cultural adaptation is applied in contemporary advertising through the analysis of campaigns developed in religious and regional contexts. The research is qualitative and exploratory, based on bibliographic review and case study analysis, seeking to understand how these strategies contribute to strengthening cultural belonging and consumer identification with brands.

latest.title: Percepción de contenidos visuales de marca en redes sociales
latest.venue: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual
latest.abstract: Las redes sociales se han convertido en un escenario fundamental para la comunicación visual de marca, ya que configuran la identidad y el posicionamiento de las mismas. Este estudio analiza cómo 385 estudiantes universitarios de Lima Sur (Perú) evalúan los contenidos visuales de marca en las plataformas digitales, centrándose en la coherencia estética, la calidad visual y la autenticidad narrativa percibida. Mediante un diseño explicativo cuantitativo y un modelo de ecuaciones estructurales de mínimos cuadrados parciales (PLS-SEM), los resultados muestran que las tres dimensiones predicen de forma positiva y significativa las respuestas actitudinales relacionadas con la marca, siendo la autenticidad percibida la que ejerce el efecto más marcado. Estos hallazgos subrayan la relevancia de las estrategias visuales con resonancia cultural para el público joven en contextos urbanos emergentes.

latest.title: A IMPORTÂNCIA DA COMUNICAÇÃO INTEGRADA DE MARKETING NO RELACIONAMENTO COM O CLIENTE
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: Integrated marketing communication has become an essential strategy for organizations seeking to strengthen relationships with their customers in an increasingly competitive market. This study aims to analyze how integrated marketing communication contributes to improving the relationship between companies and consumers. The methodology used consisted of a literature review based on books and scientific articles in the marketing field. The results indicate that the integration of advertising, sales and customer service contributes to more efficient communication, strengthens brand image and improves the consumer experience. It is concluded that companies that adopt integrated communication strategies are able to establish stronger and more lasting relationships with their customers.

latest.title: Navigating Skepticism: The Impact of Greenwashing on Brand Loyalty
latest.abstract: As consumers become increasingly environmentally conscious, brands have pivoted toward sustainability narratives to build trust and secure loyalty. However, the prevalence of greenwashing—misleading claims about environmental practices—has generated significant consumer skepticism. This research investigates how perceived greenwashing impacts brand loyalty, examining the mediating roles of consumer skepticism, brand trust, and perceived betrayal. Using qualitative secondary data analysis, the study synthesizes findings from peer-reviewed articles, industry reports, and case studies published between 2020 and 2026. Results indicate that greenwashing consistently erodes brand loyalty by damaging trust, increasing skepticism, and triggering negative word-of-mouth. The study further identifies that authenticity, third-party certifications, and transparent communication serve as critical buffers against these effects. Findings underscore the necessity for brands to adopt genuine sustainability practices and communicate them credibly to maintain long-term consumer relationships in an increasingly eco-conscious marketplace.

latest.title: A Story to Sell: The Mediating Role of Storytelling in Consumer Purchase Intention toward Regional Woven Fabrics
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study examines the associations of Perceived Government Support and influencer marketing with consumer purchase intention toward traditional woven fabrics from East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, considering storytelling as a mediating variable. Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative survey involving 347 consumers of East Nusa Tenggara woven fabrics was conducted. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess direct and indirect relationships. Finding/Results – Perceived Government Support showed no significant direct association with purchase intention (β = 0.049; p = 0.433) but was positively associated with storytelling (β = 0.574; p < 0.001). Influencer marketing positively related to storytelling (β = 0.222; p = 0.019) and purchase intention (β = 0.166; p = 0.002). Storytelling significantly predicted purchase intention (β = 0.695; p < 0.001) and demonstrated indirect-only mediation for government support (β = 0.399; p < 0.001) and complementary mediation for influencer marketing (β = 0.154; p = 0.012). Originality/Value – This study integrates government support, influencer marketing, and cultural storytelling into a unified framework explaining purchase intention toward traditional cultural products. It highlights storytelling as a strategic marketing approach for governments and SMEs while providing a foundation for future cross-cultural and longitudinal research.

latest.title: Pengaruh Lifestyle dan Impulsive Buying terhadap Keputusan Pem-belian Konsumen Smartphone Apple di Kota Depok
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of lifestyle and impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously, on the purchasing decisions of Apple smartphone consumers in Depok City. The urgency of this study arises from the limited research directly examining the relationship between lifestyle, impulsive buying, and purchasing decisions without incorporating mediating variables such as purchase intention, particularly among consumers in Depok City. This study employed an associative quantitative approach with a survey design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 96 respondents who had previously purchased Apple smartphones and resided in Depok City. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, while the sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula. The collected data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, and hypothesis testing (t-test and F-test) with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The results revealed that lifestyle had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 5.426, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Impulsive buying also had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 8.971, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, lifestyle and impulsive buying had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated F-value of 263.973, exceeding the critical F-value of 3.09, and a significance value of 0.000. These two variables collectively explained 85.0% of the variance in purchasing decisions. These findings suggest that companies

latest.title: From Visual Elements to Emotions and Trust: The Impact of Green Instagram Advertisements on Purchase Intention
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of visual elements of green advertisements on young adults’ emotional value, green trust, and subsequently purchase intention. It focuses on four visual elements commonly found in Instagram advertisements: colour, design, typography, and visual effects.
